sections.heading: Version 0.8.10.562 — August 10
sections.text: The latest official patch targets ranch and vehicle stability. It fixes animals disappearing when entering a barn or coop at night, chicks disappearing or getting stuck while growing, newborn mammals not appearing, animals missing after a load, and animals stuck between a building and its doors. It also fixes roped animals freezing after subway travel or becoming stuck outside the vet.

sections.heading: Version 0.8.10.562 — August 10
sections.text: Other fixes include vehicles becoming unresponsive at the AutoHue entrance, roof hiding on garage foundations, Steam Families detection, and the misleading incubator message “Failed to hatch,” which now reads “Infertile.” Older animal-disappearance workarounds are therefore historical context; only a reproduction on 0.8.10.562 or later should be treated as a current residual bug.

sections.heading: Version 0.8.10.455 — July 30
sections.text: The launch hotfix addressed two blockers: Steam Offline Mode could stay on a loading screen, and some players could not join a friend's co-op session. Solo play does not require a permanent internet connection; online features still require Steam to be signed in and online.

sections.heading: Vehicles, parking, and fast travel
sections.text: The smartphone's My Garage app lists owned vehicles and handles recovery. Broken, destroyed, drowned, or stuck vehicles can be sent to the mechanic, then returned to the nearest Car Pound parking location.

sections.heading: Vehicles, parking, and fast travel
sections.text: Do not leave vehicles anywhere overnight. The official update says vehicles outside your ranch or a designated Overnight Parking location can be impounded. The map currently includes 17 overnight parking locations.

sections.heading: Vehicles, parking, and fast travel
sections.text: Stolen vehicles need new license plates at AutoHue before My Garage can manage them. A stolen vehicle with forged plates can be permanently seized if left outside approved parking.

sections.heading: Vehicles, parking, and fast travel
sections.text: Sunvale has 15 subway stations after eight were added in the June update. Attached or roped animals can travel with you; version 0.8.10.562 fixed a freeze affecting roped animals after subway travel. Selected main quests also offer a skip-driving option for the vehicle, passengers, NPCs, and farm animals.

description: Avoid the most common beginner mistakes in The Ranchers: overspending early, buying animals too soon, ignoring co-op roles, wasting travel time, and planting without a plan.

sections.heading: The Ranchers Beginner Mistakes: 12 Things to Avoid in Your First Week
sections.text: The live Early Access balance may change with patches, but several preventable problems are already clear: expanding before measuring upkeep, repeating avoidable travel, parking illegally, planning around roadmap features, or letting a co-op group spend without coordination.

sections.heading: The Ranchers Beginner Mistakes: 12 Things to Avoid in Your First Week
sections.text: This page is editorial strategy , not a list of verified mechanics: each item is a recommendation built on officially confirmed systems and labeled evidence, and unverified underlying rules are flagged inside the item. Treat it as a checklist of what to be careful about, not as documented game behavior.

sections.heading: 1. Spending before you know the map
sections.text: The first shop you find is not automatically the shop you should build your plan around. Before buying anything large, learn where seeds, animals, building upgrades, and sell points are. A profitable loop on paper can become bad if it requires too much daily travel.

sections.heading: 2. Buying animals too early
sections.text: Animals are attractive because they feel like progress: a barn, a routine, a daily product. The trap is that animals usually combine several costs at once: purchase price, housing, feed, tools, and time. Buy your first animal only after crop income covers upkeep with room to spare.

sections.heading: 3. Treating sell price as profit
sections.text: A high sell price does not mean a good investment. Profit depends on seed cost, growth time, yield, processing time, and repeatability. Use profit per in-game day as the baseline. The profit calculator exists for exactly this reason.

sections.heading: 4. Reinvesting everything with no reserve
sections.text: Putting every coin into seeds feels efficient until a tool upgrade, quest item, animal feed purchase, or building fee appears. Keep a cash reserve. A slower plan that survives surprises is better than a perfect plan that collapses after one unexpected expense.

sections.heading: 5. Planting more than you can water
sections.text: A huge starter field can be worse than a small one if watering consumes the entire morning. Expand fields only when your tool upgrades, layout, or co-op help can support the routine. A maintained field compounds; a neglected field merely looks ambitious.

sections.heading: 6. Ignoring parking and fast travel
sections.text: Vehicles left outside your ranch or 17 designated Overnight Parking locations can be impounded. Learn My Garage, Car Pound recovery, and the 15 subway stations before turning every errand into a long drive.

sections.heading: 7. Starting new chores late in the day
sections.text: Late-day projects create messy days: unfinished clearing, missed NPC schedules, and panic trips to town before shops close. Use mornings for chores that must be done, afternoons for exploration and errands, and evenings for low-risk cleanup.

sections.heading: 8. Planning around roadmap features
sections.text: Mines, combat, monsters, wildlife, and hunting are listed as future updates. Build your first-week plan around mechanics visible in the current Early Access build, not the long-term feature list.

sections.heading: 9. Letting everyone spend shared money
sections.text: Co-op ranches fail when four players make four separate plans with one pool of money — and whether the wallet is literally shared is still unverified in the current build, so test it before you rely on it. Either way, choose a quartermaster for large purchases. Everyone can suggest upgrades, but one person should approve spending that affects the whole ranch.

sections.heading: 10. Duplicating chores
sections.text: If two players water the same area while nobody checks shops, co-op becomes wasted labor. Split responsibilities by domain: crops, animals, town errands, gathering, and building. Rotate roles weekly if people get bored.

sections.heading: 11. Assuming save behavior without testing it
sections.text: The official launch notes do not document world transfer or guest inventory behavior. Run a short save-and-rejoin test before a group commits hours to one ranch, and keep the session owner consistent meanwhile.

sections.heading: 12. Playing co-op without a first-session goal
sections.text: A vague "let's just play" session turns into everyone wandering. A good first co-op goal is concrete: finish the tutorial, locate key shops, plant a starter field, and agree on the first building target. Chaos is fun only after the ranch has a foundation.

sections.heading: How to recover from a bad start
sections.text: If your first week goes poorly, do not restart immediately. Most ranch-sim mistakes are recoverable if you stop expanding and rebuild the loop.

sections.heading: How to recover from a bad start
sections.text: Freeze big purchases. Do not buy animals, buildings, or decorations until cash flow is stable.

sections.heading: How to recover from a bad start
sections.text: Sell idle items. If something is sitting in storage without a clear use, turn it into money.

sections.heading: How to recover from a bad start
sections.text: Shrink the routine. Maintain a smaller field perfectly instead of a large field badly.

sections.heading: How to recover from a bad start
sections.text: Pick one income source. Run one crop cycle or one side activity until it produces reliable cash.

sections.heading: How to recover from a bad start
sections.text: Use the calculator. Enter real prices once you have them and compare options by profit/day instead of instinct.

sections.heading: Beginner mistakes FAQ
sections.text: Is it bad to buy animals in the first week?

sections.heading: Beginner mistakes FAQ
sections.text: Not always, but it is risky if you cannot cover housing and upkeep comfortably. Crops usually create a safer first money loop because the costs are smaller and faster to repeat.

sections.heading: Beginner mistakes FAQ
sections.text: Should I restart if I wasted my first few days?

sections.heading: Beginner mistakes FAQ
sections.text: Usually no. Stop spending, simplify the routine, sell excess items, and rebuild around one reliable income loop. Restart only if you want a cleaner learning run.

sections.heading: Beginner mistakes FAQ
sections.text: What is the safest first-week goal?

sections.heading: Beginner mistakes FAQ
sections.text: Finish the tutorial, plant a manageable starter field, locate key shops, keep a cash reserve, and avoid large purchases until real upkeep numbers are known.

title: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide — First 7 Days, Systems & Mistakes
description: The complete beginner's guide to The Ranchers: a day-by-day first-week roadmap, resource priorities, every announced gameplay system explained, the 10 most common beginner mistakes, and FAQ. Updated for the July 30, 2026 Steam Early Access launch.

sections.heading: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide: Your First Week on the Ranch
sections.text: Reviewed for Early Access 0.8.10.562 · August 11, 2026 · Reading time: ~17 min

sections.heading: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide: Your First Week on the Ranch
sections.text: Your first 30 minutes

sections.heading: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide: Your First Week on the Ranch
sections.text: Known gameplay systems, explained

sections.heading: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide: Your First Week on the Ranch
sections.text: The 10 most common beginner mistakes

sections.heading: Before starting: mode and transport
sections.text: Check the build only when troubleshooting. The current official version reviewed here is 0.8.10.562. Solo can run with Steam Offline Mode; co-op still needs Steam sign-in and internet.

sections.heading: Before starting: mode and transport
sections.text: Follow the opening questline. It introduces the ranch, first fields, seed buying, early home crafting, villagers, shops, and driving. First-use tutorials appear when you attempt a new mechanic.

sections.heading: Before starting: mode and transport
sections.text: Learn transport before expanding. Sunvale currently has 15 subway stations. Roped or attached animals can travel with you, and selected quest drives can be skipped with passengers and animals included.

sections.heading: Before starting: mode and transport
sections.text: Protect your vehicle. Park at your ranch or one of 17 Overnight Parking locations. Otherwise it may be impounded. My Garage can send damaged or stuck vehicles to a mechanic and route them back through a Car Pound.

sections.heading: Your first 7 days: a day-by-day roadmap
sections.text: The opening should establish orientation and a maintainable routine. The sequence below is editorial advice built around current official systems, not a claim that one crop or purchase has already been mathematically solved.

sections.heading: Day 1 — Scout, don't spend
sections.text: Follow the main quest until the ranch, driving, shops, and first-use tutorials are clear. Mark the nearest subway and legal overnight parking. Delay large purchases until you understand the route between ranch and town.

sections.heading: Day 2 — Plant your first money loop
sections.text: Use a small plot to learn the current plantation loop. Record the seed cost, planting day, harvest day, yield, quality, and sale channel. The official notes confirm that unharvested produce remains and recurring crops have a regrow flow.

sections.heading: Day 3 — Follow the quest threads
sections.text: Continue the main quest and first-use tutorials. Failed quests can be replayed with state resets, so learning a mechanic is safer than abandoning the questline to chase an assumed optimal route.

sections.heading: Day 4 — Start a second skill
sections.text: Explore one secondary activity that is available in your current build, but do not plan around roadmap systems. The developer lists mines, combat, monsters, wildlife, and hunting as future content rather than launch features.

sections.heading: Day 5 — First harvest, first reinvestment
sections.text: When the first crop is ready, record its yield, quality and available sale values before deciding what to keep. Protect the exact cost of repeating the crop cycle; use only the surplus for expansion or experiments.

sections.heading: Day 6 — Expand the plot, meet the town
sections.text: Clear and till a second field only if the first remains manageable. In the afternoon, make a deliberate town loop: check the daily orders and local markets, note who sells what, and record useful routes. Do not assume gifts, discounts or relationship rewards until the current build shows them.

sections.heading: Day 7 — Plan your first animal purchase
sections.text: End the week by doing math, not shopping. Check what your crops actually earned per day in your save. Before buying an animal, record its housing, feed and tool requirements; delay the purchase if those costs are still unknown.

sections.heading: Opening quest chains (video-observed)
sections.text: The quest steps below were read directly off the screen of a public playthrough of the current build (Games Station, V0.8.10.455, Spring Year 1 Days 4–8) Video-observed . Day numbers mark when each chain was active in that single playthrough — your own pacing can differ.

sections.heading: Feathered Foes — active on Day 4
sections.text: Objective: craft 1 scarecrow . Scarecrow recipes live in the workbench crafting menu (see the building guide ).

sections.heading: Rust to Rumbling! — active on Day 5
sections.text: Save at least 3,000C in your bank.

sections.heading: Rust to Rumbling! — active on Day 5
sections.text: Repair Victor's old car.

sections.heading: Rust to Rumbling! — active on Day 5
sections.text: Take a bike from a Bykii terminal in the meantime.

sections.heading: Rust to Rumbling! — active on Day 5
sections.text: Pick up your new car.

sections.heading: Power to the Bench — active on Day 8
sections.text: Have at least 1,000C in your bank.

sections.heading: Power to the Bench — active on Day 8
sections.text: Sign an electricity contract with Victor.

sections.heading: Power to the Bench — active on Day 8
sections.text: Build a workbench in your ranch (the build runs in 5 steps).

sections.heading: Power to the Bench — active on Day 8
sections.text: Check your ranch's energy usage.

sections.heading: Power to the Bench — active on Day 8
sections.text: Who is Victor? City Hall dialogue identifies him as "Victor, Sunvale's Mayor" Video-observed , and his NPC profile shows a 5-heart friendship bar. The electricity contract in Power to the Bench is signed with him at City Hall — see the electricity & water guide .

sections.heading: Two more video-observed mechanic clues
sections.text: Tutorials arrive by phone. Meriam coaches the workbench flow through a phone call — gather the basic materials first, then place the workbench Video-observed Games Station, 30:55 . Answer your phone; tutorial guidance is pushed to you there, not only through quest markers.

sections.heading: Two more video-observed mechanic clues
sections.text: Heavy labor drains health, not just time. In the same playthrough, a Day-7 woodcutting session dropped the player to 40/80 health and began deducting health Video-observed . The exact threshold and drain rate are unobserved — treat long gathering sessions as a health-cost activity and carry food (the observed Green Salad restores 20 health / 30 energy).

sections.heading: Resource priorities: what matters first
sections.text: With limited money, energy, and daylight, the order you invest in things matters more than the things themselves. Our recommended priority stack for the first month:

sections.heading: Resource priorities: what matters first
sections.text: Time-saving infrastructure. Anything that reduces walking, watering, or inventory trips pays for itself every single day. A well-placed chest or a closer field layout is worth more than a shinier tool.

sections.heading: Resource priorities: what matters first
sections.text: Seed capital. Money that becomes more money within one crop cycle outranks everything except survival purchases.

sections.heading: Resource priorities: what matters first
sections.text: Tool upgrades. Compare the displayed or observed effect before buying. Prioritize an upgrade only when it removes a real daily bottleneck.

sections.heading: Resource priorities: what matters first
sections.text: Animals. Only once crops cover upkeep with margin.

sections.heading: Resource priorities: what matters first
sections.text: Decorations and cosmetics. Last. Always last.

sections.heading: Known gameplay systems, explained
sections.text: Official material establishes the broad pillars below. Practical suggestions are editorial advice; exact energy costs, crop restrictions, upgrade effects and relationship rewards require current-build observations.

sections.heading: Energy and time
sections.text: Watch the current build's clock and player-status UI before planning a full day. Record which actions consume time or energy, then put mandatory chores first and leave a travel buffer for town errands.

sections.heading: Energy and time
sections.text: Official The day does not roll over on its own: a new day starts only when you press the "Start new day" button in the end-of-the-day summary — and that, per the pre-EA Ranching v2 update notes, is how you pause the game; the notes say it also works in multiplayer. This is pre-EA official documentation not yet independently rechecked in the current EA build — worth a one-minute test in your own save. Practically: you can linger on the summary screen to plan or step away without the clock advancing.

sections.heading: Tools and upgrades
sections.text: The opening quest and first-use tutorials introduce available tools. Check each upgrade's current description and test its effect before spending; the site does not assume tiers, energy savings or unlock conditions that the live build has not documented.

sections.heading: Seasons and crops
sections.text: The game advertises seasons, but complete live-build crop restrictions are still being documented. Read each seed listing, record the season label, and test what happens at a season boundary before buying large quantities. The crop database separates confirmed mechanics from pending measurements.

sections.heading: Town, NPCs, and relationships
sections.text: The official material confirms shops, daily orders, local markets, quests, and resident interactions. Record actual opening hours and requirements instead of assuming gifts, discounts, or birthday multipliers that have not been verified.

sections.heading: Town, NPCs, and relationships
sections.text: Where seeds and fertilizer actually are: the Leafy Market shop is organized into four tabs — Seed & Fertilizer, Vegetables, Grocery, and Weaponry (Temporary) — and seeds and fertilizer sit on the first tab Video-observed Games Station, 03:15–03:55 . This is a single-playthrough observation of the current build (0.8.10.455): it tells you where to look for seeds on Day 2, not a full price list.

sections.heading: Building and ranch expansion
sections.text: Official descriptions include house construction, animal facilities, fences, sprinklers, greenhouses and utility systems. Check the current recipe and unlock requirements before choosing a target, then keep enough cash and materials to maintain the activities already running.

sections.heading: Co-op
sections.text: The game supports 1–4 player online co-op. Steam sign-in and internet are required for online features. If joining fails, confirm both players are on the same current build; 0.8.10.455 fixed an early join issue, while the current reviewed version is 0.8.10.562.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: This list is editorial strategy built on the confirmed systems above, not a set of verified mechanics. Where the underlying behavior still needs current-build evidence, the item says so.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Buying animals before you can feed them. The animal, its housing, and its daily upkeep are all likely to cost money before it produces anything. Until upkeep costs are observed in your build, fund livestock from surplus, not hope.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Planting out of season. Season limits by crop are not yet fully documented in the current build, so check the seed description before planting across seasons and run a small boundary test before committing your budget.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Hoarding harvests. Produce sitting in a chest is not earning anything; the editorial advice is to sell, reinvest, repeat — though exact spoilage or storage rules need current-build checks.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Skipping the quests. The opening quest introduces core locations and mechanics, and failed quests can be replayed with an automatic state reset.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Overplanting your watering capacity. Whether under-watered crops grow slower in the current build is unverified; until you have observed the watering rule, scale planting to what your morning routine can actually tend.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Ignoring travel time. The distant buyer paying slightly more is usually a worse deal after the round trip. Sell close unless the margin is dramatic.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Upgrading the wrong tool first. Upgrade what you use every day, not what looks coolest.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Running out of energy at noon. Heavy labor has an observed health cost in the current build Video-observed , so budget stamina like money: heavy chores early, light chores late, eat when you can.

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Neglecting the town. Editorial strategy: relationship rewards are not yet documented in the current build, but meeting NPCs early costs little and quests already route through them — Victor (the Mayor) gates the electricity contract Video-observed .

sections.heading: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
sections.text: Expanding before stabilizing. One boring, reliable income loop beats three exciting half-built ones. Grow what works until it's automatic, then diversify.

sections.heading: Beginner FAQ
sections.text: What's the very first thing I should do in The Ranchers?

sections.heading: Beginner FAQ
sections.text: Check the build number, follow the opening quest, locate the nearest subway and legal parking, then start a small crop test whose full cost and yield you can record.

sections.heading: Beginner FAQ
sections.text: Should I play solo or in co-op first?

sections.heading: Beginner FAQ
sections.text: Both are fully supported. Solo teaches you the systems at your own pace; co-op (1–4 players) multiplies your labor but adds coordination overhead. If your group is new, have everyone skim this guide and the co-op guide first.

sections.heading: Beginner FAQ
sections.text: How do I make money fast at the start?

sections.heading: Beginner FAQ
sections.text: No universal route is verified yet. Record the activities available in your save and compare net profit per day plus active labor with the method in the money guide .

sections.heading: Beginner FAQ

title: Before starting: mode and transport
parentTitle: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide — First 7 Days, Systems & Mistakes
description: Check the build only when troubleshooting. The current official version reviewed here is 0.8.10.562. Solo can run with Steam Offline Mode; co-op still needs Steam sign-in and internet. Learn transport before expanding. Sunvale currently has 15 subway stations. Roped or attached animals can travel with you, and selected quest drives can be skipped with passengers and animals included. Protect your vehicle. title: Resource priorities: what matters first
parentTitle: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide — First 7 Days, Systems & Mistakes
description: With limited money, energy, and daylight, the order you invest in things matters more than the things themselves. Our recommended priority stack for the first month: Time-saving infrastructure. Anything that reduces walking, watering, or inventory trips pays for itself every single day. A well-placed chest or a closer field layout is worth more than a shinier tool. Seed capital. Money that becomes more money within one crop cycle outranks everything except survival purchases. Tool upgrades. Compare the displayed or observed effect before buying. Prioritize an upgrade only when it removes a real daily bottleneck. Animals. Only once crops cover upkeep with margin. Decorations and cosmetics. Last. Always last.

title: Energy and time
parentTitle: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide — First 7 Days, Systems & Mistakes
description: Watch the current build's clock and player-status UI before planning a full day. Record which actions consume time or energy, then put mandatory chores first and leave a travel buffer for town errands. Official The day does not roll over on its own: a new day starts only when you press the "Start new day" button in the end-of-the-day summary — and that, per the pre-EA Ranching v2 update notes, is how you pause the game; the notes say it also works in multiplayer. This is pre-EA official documentation not yet independently rechecked in the current EA build — worth a one-minute test in your own save. Practically: you can linger on the summary screen to plan or step away without the clock advancing.

title: The 10 most common beginner mistakes
parentTitle: The Ranchers Beginner's Guide — First 7 Days, Systems & Mistakes
description: This list is editorial strategy built on the confirmed systems above, not a set of verified mechanics. Where the underlying behavior still needs current-build evidence, the item says so. Buying animals before you can feed them. The animal, its housing, and its daily upkeep are all likely to cost money before it produces anything. Until upkeep costs are observed in your build, fund livestock from surplus, not hope. Planting out of season. Season limits by crop are not yet fully documented in the current build, so check the seed description before planting across seasons and run a small boundary test before committing your budget. Hoarding harvests. Produce sitting in a chest is not earning anything; the editorial advice is to sell, reinvest, repeat — though exact spoilage or storage rules need current-build checks. Skipping the quests. The opening quest introduces core locations and mechanics, and failed quests can be replayed with an automatic state reset. Overplanting your watering capacity. Whether under-watered crops grow slower in the current build is unverified; until you have observed the watering rule, scale planting to what your morning routine can actually tend. Ignoring travel time. The distant buyer paying slightly more is usually a worse deal after the round trip. Sell close unless the margin is dramatic. Upgrading the wrong tool first. Upgrade what you use every day, not what looks coolest. Running out of energy at noon. Heavy labor has an observed health cost in the current build Video-observed , so budget stamina like money: heavy chores early, light chores late, eat when you can. Neglecting the town. Editorial strategy: relationship rewards are not yet documented in the current build, but meeting NPCs early costs little and quests already route through them — Victor (the Mayor) gates the electricity contract Video-observed . Expanding before stabilizing. One boring, reliable income loop beats three exciting half-built ones. Grow what works until it's automatic, then diversify.

Deposits do not pay immediately; crop income appears on the end-of-day Farming line. Stop and use a focused fix when blocked: roof quest , missing vehicle , chicken care , or Gigi's large egg .

sections.heading: The direct answer

(The prices on this page are tied to a named build, source and timestamp.) What works right now, regardless of patch:

sections.heading: The formulas: profit per day, per minute, payback
sections.text: The three formulas used across this entire site:

sections.heading: The formulas: profit per day, per minute, payback
sections.text: Crops: profit per plot per day = (sell price × yield − seed cost) ÷ growth days

sections.heading: The formulas: profit per day, per minute, payback
sections.text: Animals: profit per animal per day = (product price × products per cycle − feed/upkeep per cycle) ÷ cycle days

sections.heading: The formulas: profit per day, per minute, payback
sections.text: Upgrades: payback days = total startup cost ÷ additional net profit per day

sections.heading: The formulas: profit per day, per minute, payback
sections.text: Use two rates, because each answers a different question. Profit per in-game day shows how efficiently land, housing, or a machine slot is used. Profit per active minute shows how efficiently your own attention is used — two activities can return the same profit per day while one consumes an entire morning. Record travel separately, especially when comparing a local sale with a distant buyer.

sections.heading: Crops: measure a complete cycle
sections.text: Record seed cost, planting date, first harvest, regrow interval, yield, quality and sale value. Official notes confirm recurring crops, persistent unharvested produce and a Luck effect on fruit counts Official , so one harvest is not enough for a reliable ranking. If a crop regrows, split the first harvest from later harvests because the seed cost applies differently.

sections.heading: Livestock: include the full setup
sections.text: Do not compare product revenue with crop profit while ignoring the animal, housing, feed or care time. Official notes say Luck can affect newborn quality Official , so breeding results also need several observations before they support a recommendation.

sections.heading: Processing: compare against the input's value
sections.text: For any available recipe, subtract the value you could have received by selling the inputs directly. Then include machine cost, batch size and processing time. A higher final sale price does not automatically mean a better return.

sections.heading: Active work: measure the whole route
sections.text: Official One route you can cross off the list: you cannot currently make money by selling vehicles — stolen ones included — though the developers say the option is planned (see selling vehicles ).

sections.heading: Active work: measure the whole route
sections.text: For fishing or any other active task available in your build, start a timer when you leave the ranch and stop after the sale. Include travel, inventory management and failed attempts. This makes the comparison fair against chores that continue producing while you do something else.

sections.heading: How to measure: the observation sheet
sections.text: Start one row per activity, item, animal, or structure. Give every row a source type: official description, direct observation, or community lead. Only versioned direct observations should fill build-specific numbers.

sections.heading: How to measure: the observation sheet
sections.text: Context: game version, date observed, single-player or co-op, season, and difficulty setting if one exists.

sections.heading: How to measure: the observation sheet
sections.text: Inputs: purchase cost, recurring materials, utilities, feed, seed, market fee, and required structure share.

sections.heading: How to measure: the observation sheet
sections.text: Outputs: quantity, quality, base sale value, sale channel, and any processing step.

sections.heading: How to measure: the observation sheet
sections.text: Time: in-game cycle length, active player minutes, travel time, and time blocked by capacity.

sections.heading: How to measure: the observation sheet
sections.text: Evidence: screenshot, short clip, or exact sequence another player can repeat.

sections.heading: How to measure: the observation sheet
sections.text: Keep unknown fields empty. Zero means the tested value is zero; blank means it has not been measured. That distinction prevents incomplete data from turning into a false ranking. For crops, begin with a control plot and no optional bonus. For animals, measure at least two complete cycles before ranking a product, and keep missed-care tests in a separate save so they do not contaminate the baseline.

sections.heading: Selling channels: orders, local markets, auction
sections.text: Official material describes daily orders, local markets, and an auction market Official . It does not guarantee that one channel always pays more. Compare them using the same item, quality, quantity, and game version:

sections.heading: Selling channels: orders, local markets, auction
sections.text: Record gross price, fees, quantity limits, delivery requirements, and payment delay.

sections.heading: Selling channels: orders, local markets, auction
sections.text: Include travel and menu time in active labor.

sections.heading: Selling channels: orders, local markets, auction
sections.text: Separate a guaranteed offer from a player-dependent auction result.

sections.heading: Selling channels: orders, local markets, auction
sections.text: Repeat time-sensitive observations before describing a stable price pattern.

sections.heading: How to sell crops: the CashIn chest
sections.text: Quick answer: sell your harvest through the CashIn Export Storage Chest next to the Cargo/helipad paved area on your ranch. Depositing crops pays nothing on the spot — the money arrives in that day's end-of-day settlement, on the Farming line. Observed in EA 0.8.10.455.

sections.heading: How to sell crops: the CashIn chest
sections.text: Harvest and carry your crops to the CashIn chest by the Cargo/helipad area.

sections.heading: How to sell crops: the CashIn chest
sections.text: Transfer them into the chest — your wallet does not change at this point, and that is normal, not a bug.

sections.heading: How to sell crops: the CashIn chest
sections.text: Sleep and check the settlement screen. Crop income appears as one combined Farming total (observed example: Day 8, Farming +1,534).

sections.heading: How to sell crops: the CashIn chest
sections.text: Two consequences worth knowing before you go price-hunting. First, the settlement does not break the Farming line down per crop , so per-crop sell prices cannot be read off it — which is why no per-crop sell prices are published on this site yet. Second, if you deposited crops and "got no money," check the next morning's settlement before assuming a bug.

sections.heading: How to sell crops: the CashIn chest
sections.text: One more possible channel: Meriam, the architect at City Hall, has a "Sell items" dialogue option. It was not used in the observed playthrough, so treat it as an unverified lead, not a confirmed shop. Observed in EA 0.8.10.455.

sections.heading: How to sell crops: the CashIn chest
sections.text: Map entry: Cash-In box on the Sunvale map .

sections.heading: Utility income: selling surplus power
sections.text: The official Steam description says players can use wells, wind turbines, and solar panels, and can sell surplus power Official . To evaluate that system, record equipment cost, output by time and weather, ranch consumption, sale rate, maintenance, and grid limits.

sections.heading: Utility income: selling surplus power
sections.text: Only surplus is revenue. Power consumed by sprinklers, buildings, or other equipment is an avoided purchase or operating benefit, not a second sale. Keep those two benefits separate to avoid double-counting. Player reports that surplus sale payouts are unclear remain open Unverified lead — see the research queue and the electricity guide .

sections.heading: Reinvestment pacing: the 3-bucket rule
sections.text: This is an editorial budgeting method, not an in-game rule. Separate each meaningful payout into three buckets:

sections.heading: Reinvestment pacing: the 3-bucket rule
sections.text: Operating: the verified cost of repeating your current cycle.

sections.heading: Reinvestment pacing: the 3-bucket rule
sections.text: Growth: an upgrade whose cost and benefit you have already checked.

sections.heading: Reinvestment pacing: the 3-bucket rule
sections.text: Reserve: money left after the first two buckets for mistakes, quests and patch surprises.

sections.heading: Reinvestment pacing: the 3-bucket rule
sections.text: Use actual costs instead of a fixed percentage. If the next cycle costs 600, protect 600 first. Only the remaining amount is available for expansion.

sections.heading: Seasonal cash planning
sections.text: Seasonal systems are advertised Official , but exact crop behavior must be checked in the current build. Before a transition:

sections.heading: Seasonal cash planning
sections.text: Read the seed listing. Record its displayed season and growth duration.

sections.heading: Seasonal cash planning
sections.text: Run one boundary test. Observe what happens to a planted crop when the season changes.

sections.heading: Seasonal cash planning
sections.text: Keep a control sample. Compare the same crop within a stable part of the season.

sections.heading: Seasonal cash planning
sections.text: Delay large assumptions. Do not pre-buy or discard stock until the current build confirms how storage and season changes behave.

sections.heading: Money in co-op: the economy split
sections.text: Co-op supports 1–4 players Official , so a crew can test parallel tasks. Measure the same route once solo and once with a crew before assuming the output scales linearly; travel, shared tools and duplicated work can erase the apparent gain.

sections.heading: Money in co-op: the economy split
sections.text: Record total player-minutes rather than elapsed clock time. Four players finishing a task quickly may still spend more combined labor. Agree who records purchases and sale results: a single ledger prevents the same expense being counted twice. The full session workflow is in the co-op guide .

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text: First days: use measured no-capital work while your first crop cycle grows. The retained example is foraging: 692C on Day 4 and 1,272C on Day 6 Video-observed — one session, not a stable daily rate or a proven optimum. Fishing remains unranked until its payout is measured.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text: First expansion: buy only what you have already measured — one candidate, one control cycle, one repeat. Multi-harvest crops (strawberry confirmed in the current build) spread their seed cost across repeat harvests, so judge them per harvest, not per planting.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text: First animal: after you can cover the animal, its housing share, and a reserve for recurring care without blocking essential progress.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text: Processing: only when the increase over direct-sale input value covers machine cost and processing time.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text: Upgrades: rank them by payback days. If a sprinkler changes active labor but not crop revenue, value it by minutes saved and the extra work those minutes allow.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text: Cash reserve: keep at least the verified cost of repeating your current production cycle, plus a separate buffer for known quest, feed or repair costs.

sections.heading: Recommendations
sections.text: The five-step test behind every recommendation: choose one candidate with build, season, quality and sale channel fixed; run a control cycle recording every input, output, elapsed day and active minute; repeat it; change one variable; compare net results per day and per active minute.

sections.heading: Known limits
sections.text: The 3-bucket rule and the recommendations are editorial planning methods, not hidden game mechanics.

sections.heading: Known limits
sections.text: Auction results depend on other players, so they cannot be reproduced like a vendor price.

sections.heading: Known limits
sections.text: If two sources give you different numbers for the same item, report both — our conflict rule is to show conflicting values side by side, not to silently pick one.

sections.heading: Known limits
sections.text: Share reproducible observations through the contact page . Include the version and a screenshot so a result can be checked before it becomes public data.

sections.text: What's the fastest way to make money early in The Ranchers?

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: The only no-capital route here with retained income screens is foraging: one playthrough showed 692C on Day 4 and 1,272C on Day 6. Use that as a testable starting point, not a promised daily rate. Fishing remains unranked until a current payout is measured.

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: Are crops or animals more profitable?

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: Compare a full crop cycle with the animal's purchase, housing, feed, care time and product cycle. The answer can change with progression, quality, Luck and patches.

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: Is processing worth it?

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: Only when the increase over direct-sale input value covers machine cost and processing time. Test one recipe with the same input quality and sale channel before scaling it.

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: Should I sell to vendors or the auction market?

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: Test the same item in each available channel. Compare net price after fees, quantity limits, delivery work, payment delay, and the reliability of finding a buyer.

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: When should I buy my first animal?

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: After you can cover the animal, its housing share, and a reserve for recurring care without blocking essential progress. Use observed costs rather than a fixed calendar date.

sections.heading: Money-making FAQ
sections.text: Co-op enables parallel work, but the gain depends on ownership rules, shared tools, travel, and coordination. Compare elapsed time and total player-minutes for the same task.

parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: There is no verified single "best" money-maker in the current Early Access build yet — and exact prices quoted without build-specific evidence should be treated cautiously. (The prices on this page are tied to a named build, source and timestamp.) What works right now, regardless of patch: Judge every activity by profit per in-game day and profit per active minute , never by sale price per item. The formulas are below. Protect the cost of repeating your current cycle before spending on anything else — seeds, feed and fees come before expansion. Foraging is the only no-capital route here with a retained on-screen income ledger. Fishing exists, but this guide does not yet have a measured current-build payout for it. Test selling channels (daily orders, local markets, auction) with the same item before assuming one always pays more. Score upgrades by payback days , not by their sticker price or promised boost. Everything after this section shows the method, the tables to fill in, and exactly which claims are official, observed, or still open. title: The formulas: profit per day, per minute, payback
parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: The three formulas used across this entire site: Crops: profit per plot per day = (sell price × yield − seed cost) ÷ growth days Animals: profit per animal per day = (product price × products per cycle − feed/upkeep per cycle) ÷ cycle days Upgrades: payback days = total startup cost ÷ additional net profit per day Use two rates, because each answers a different question. Profit per in-game day shows how efficiently land, housing, or a machine slot is used. Profit per active minute shows how efficiently your own attention is used — two activities can return the same profit per day while one consumes an entire morning. Record travel separately, especially when comparing a local sale with a distant buyer. Enter observed values in the profit calculator . Entries stay in your browser, so you can compare your own save without sending gameplay data to us.

title: How to measure: the observation sheet
parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: Start one row per activity, item, animal, or structure. Give every row a source type: official description, direct observation, or community lead. Only versioned direct observations should fill build-specific numbers. Context: game version, date observed, single-player or co-op, season, and difficulty setting if one exists. Inputs: purchase cost, recurring materials, utilities, feed, seed, market fee, and required structure share. Outputs: quantity, quality, base sale value, sale channel, and any processing step. Time: in-game cycle length, active player minutes, travel time, and time blocked by capacity. Evidence: screenshot, short clip, or exact sequence another player can repeat. Keep unknown fields empty. Zero means the tested value is zero; blank means it has not been measured. That distinction prevents incomplete data from turning into a false ranking. For crops, begin with a control plot and no optional bonus. For animals, measure at least two complete cycles before ranking a product, and keep missed-care tests in a separate save so they do not contaminate the baseline.

title: How to sell crops: the CashIn chest
parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: Quick answer: sell your harvest through the CashIn Export Storage Chest next to the Cargo/helipad paved area on your ranch. Depositing crops pays nothing on the spot — the money arrives in that day's end-of-day settlement, on the Farming line. Observed in EA 0.8.10.455. Harvest and carry your crops to the CashIn chest by the Cargo/helipad area. Transfer them into the chest — your wallet does not change at this point, and that is normal, not a bug. Sleep and check the settlement screen. Crop income appears as one combined Farming total (observed example: Day 8, Farming +1,534). Two consequences worth knowing before you go price-hunting. First, the settlement does not break the Farming line down per crop , so per-crop sell prices cannot be read off it — which is why no per-crop sell prices are published on this site yet. Second, if you deposited crops and "got no money," check the next morning's settlement before assuming a bug. One more possible channel: Meriam, the architect at City Hall, has a "Sell items" dialogue option. It was not used in the observed playthrough, so treat it as an unverified lead, not a confirmed shop. Observed in EA 0.8.10.455. Map entry: Cash-In box on the Sunvale map .

title: Utility income: selling surplus power
parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: The official Steam description says players can use wells, wind turbines, and solar panels, and can sell surplus power Official . To evaluate that system, record equipment cost, output by time and weather, ranch consumption, sale rate, maintenance, and grid limits. Only surplus is revenue. Power consumed by sprinklers, buildings, or other equipment is an avoided purchase or operating benefit, not a second sale. Keep those two benefits separate to avoid double-counting. Player reports that surplus sale payouts are unclear remain open Unverified lead — see the research queue and the electricity guide .

title: Reinvestment pacing: the 3-bucket rule
parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: This is an editorial budgeting method, not an in-game rule. Separate each meaningful payout into three buckets: Operating: the verified cost of repeating your current cycle. Growth: an upgrade whose cost and benefit you have already checked. Reserve: money left after the first two buckets for mistakes, quests and patch surprises. Use actual costs instead of a fixed percentage. If the next cycle costs 600, protect 600 first. Only the remaining amount is available for expansion.

parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: Seasonal systems are advertised Official , but exact crop behavior must be checked in the current build. Before a transition: Read the seed listing. title: Money in co-op: the economy split
parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: Co-op supports 1–4 players Official , so a crew can test parallel tasks. Measure the same route once solo and once with a crew before assuming the output scales linearly; travel, shared tools and duplicated work can erase the apparent gain. Record total player-minutes rather than elapsed clock time. Four players finishing a task quickly may still spend more combined labor. Agree who records purchases and sale results: a single ledger prevents the same expense being counted twice. The full session workflow is in the co-op guide .

title: Recommendations
parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: First days: use measured no-capital work while your first crop cycle grows. The retained example is foraging: 692C on Day 4 and 1,272C on Day 6 Video-observed — one session, not a stable daily rate or a proven optimum. Fishing remains unranked until its payout is measured. First expansion: buy only what you have already measured — one candidate, one control cycle, one repeat. Multi-harvest crops (strawberry confirmed in the current build) spread their seed cost across repeat harvests, so judge them per harvest, not per planting. First animal: after you can cover the animal, its housing share, and a reserve for recurring care without blocking essential progress. Processing: only when the increase over direct-sale input value covers machine cost and processing time. Upgrades: rank them by payback days. If a sprinkler changes active labor but not crop revenue, value it by minutes saved and the extra work those minutes allow. Cash reserve: keep at least the verified cost of repeating your current production cycle, plus a separate buffer for known quest, feed or repair costs. The five-step test behind every recommendation: choose one candidate with build, season, quality and sale channel fixed; run a control cycle recording every input, output, elapsed day and active minute; repeat it; change one variable; compare net results per day and per active minute.

title: Money-making FAQ
parentTitle: The Ranchers Money-Making Guide — Best Income Routes, Formulas & Payback
description: What's the fastest way to make money early in The Ranchers? The only no-capital route here with retained income screens is foraging: one playthrough showed 692C on Day 4 and 1,272C on Day 6. Use that as a testable starting point, not a promised daily rate. Fishing remains unranked until a current payout is measured. Are crops or animals more profitable? Compare a full crop cycle with the animal's purchase, housing, feed, care time and product cycle. The answer can change with progression, quality, Luck and patches. Is processing worth it? Only when the increase over direct-sale input value covers machine cost and processing time. Test one recipe with the same input quality and sale channel before scaling it. Should I sell to vendors or the auction market? Test the same item in each available channel. Compare net price after fees, quantity limits, delivery work, payment delay, and the reliability of finding a buyer. When should I buy my first animal? After you can cover the animal, its housing share, and a reserve for recurring care without blocking essential progress. Use observed costs rather than a fixed calendar date. How does co-op change the money route? Co-op enables parallel work, but the gain depends on ownership rules, shared tools, travel, and coordination. Compare elapsed time and total player-minutes for the same task. Where can I compare actual crop and animal numbers? The crop and animal databases separate official facts from pending measurements. The profit calculator ranks values you observe yourself.

sections.heading: Hosting & joining: setup walkthrough
sections.text: The Ranchers supports 1–4 player online co-op. The official launch notes confirm multiplayer-ready quests, while the July 30 hotfix addresses a join failure affecting some friend sessions.

sections.text: Update together. Confirm every player is on 0.8.10.562 or later before diagnosing invitations.

sections.heading: Before anyone hosts
sections.text: Sign into Steam. Offline solo works, but co-op and other online features require an active Steam connection.

sections.heading: Before anyone hosts
sections.text: Pick a session owner deliberately. Save ownership and transfer behavior should be tested in your build before the group commits to a long shared world.

sections.heading: Before anyone hosts
sections.text: Decide the ranch's identity first. Crop-focused? Animal-heavy? A builder's paradise? Five minutes of alignment before the world is created saves a week of pulling in different directions.

sections.heading: Hosting the session
sections.text: Create or load the intended world and open its multiplayer session.

sections.heading: Hosting the session
sections.text: Invite Steam friends only after every client reports the same build.

sections.heading: Hosting the session
sections.text: Confirm all players enter the same ranch before spending shared resources or advancing quests.

sections.heading: Hosting the session
sections.text: Run one save-and-rejoin test early to learn how the current build preserves guest and world progress.

sections.heading: Hosting the session
sections.text: Do not publish assumptions about save ownership, guest inventory, or wallet sharing as facts. Test each behavior in the current build and keep the session owner consistent until the result is clear.

sections.heading: Role splits for 1–4 players
sections.text: The number one co-op failure mode in farming games isn't conflict — it's duplication : two players watering the same field while the animals go unfed. The fix is zones of ownership . Each player owns a domain end-to-end; within an in-game week, nobody touches someone else's domain without asking.

sections.heading: Solo (1 player)
sections.text: Everything is yours, so sequencing replaces splitting: crops in the morning, town and selling midday, planning and light chores in the evening. Our beginner's guide roadmap is built exactly for this.

sections.heading: Duo (2 players)
sections.text: Player 1 — Fields: tilling, planting, watering, harvesting, seed purchasing. Owns the crop calendar.

sections.heading: Duo (2 players)
sections.text: Player 2 — Everything else: animals, selling runs, shopping, quests, building. Effectively the ranch's operations manager.

sections.heading: Trio (3 players)
sections.text: Fields lead: the entire crop pipeline.

sections.heading: Trio (3 players)
sections.text: Barn lead: all livestock — feeding, collecting, care, housing repairs, feed stockpiling.

sections.heading: Trio (3 players)
sections.text: Road lead: selling, buying, quests, fishing and other active work for filler income, scouting prices.

sections.heading: Full crew (4 players)
sections.text: Fields lead: crops, sized to the crew's combined watering capacity (which is much larger — scale up boldly).

sections.heading: Full crew (4 players)
sections.text: Barn lead: livestock end-to-end. Owns the feed budget.

sections.heading: Full crew (4 players)
sections.text: Builder: construction, upgrades, layout, storage logistics. The force multiplier — a well-placed building saves the whole crew time every day.

sections.heading: Full crew (4 players)
sections.text: Quartermaster: sells everything, tracks prices, keeps the crew's money records, pre-buys next season's seeds, and approves all large purchases. The least glamorous and most important role.

sections.heading: Full crew (4 players)
sections.text: Rotate roles between in-game weeks if anyone gets restless — but within a week, stable ownership beats flexibility every time.

title: Full crew (4 players)
parentTitle: The Ranchers Multiplayer & Co-op Guide — Hosting, Roles & Schedules
description: Fields lead: crops, sized to the crew's combined watering capacity (which is much larger — scale up boldly). Barn lead: livestock end-to-end. Owns the feed budget. Builder: construction, upgrades, layout, storage logistics. The force multiplier — a well-placed building saves the whole crew time every day. Quartermaster: sells everything, tracks prices, keeps the crew's money records, pre-buys next season's seeds, and approves all large purchases. The least glamorous and most important role. Rotate roles between in-game weeks if anyone gets restless — but within a week, stable ownership beats flexibility every time.

title: The Ranchers Chicken Care Guide: Buying, Feeding, Heaters, Eggs & Profit
description: A practical chicken care walkthrough for The Ranchers Early Access: where bought chickens actually go, what to feed, which heater works and where to mount it, how large eggs happen, the full auto-feeding setup, the disappearing-chicken checklist, and how to profit from extra birds.

sections.heading: The Ranchers Animal Guide: Chickens, Step by Step
sections.text: Reviewed August 11, 2026 · Current version 0.8.10.562 · Reading time: ~12 min

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Bought chickens wait in the fenced field behind the seller Angela's house — grab them there and load the car boot. Feed hay via the trough inside the coop. Buy the coop heater/AC from Angela (the City Hall decoration version does nothing) and mount it on the outside wall . Sick bird → vet . Spare roosters can't be sold alive — dispatch and sell the meat .

sections.heading: Getting your chickens home
sections.text: Quick answer: after you buy chickens, they are not in your backpack or truck — they appear in the small fenced field behind Angela's house (Angela is the chicken seller). Walk there, grab each bird, and either load them into your car's boot or carry them home one by one on foot. Multiple player reports.

sections.heading: Getting your chickens home
sections.text: Every documented "Chicken coop mission" stuck report here came from missing the post-purchase prompt: those players never thought to look behind the seller's house. That does not rule out other mission bugs. If the field is empty or the objective still will not advance, record your build and quest screen. Angela is also the correct vendor for the coop heater and AC unit (see below).

sections.heading: Feeding chickens: hay & water
sections.text: Quick answer: chickens eat hay . Fill the trough inside the coop — animals eat and drink once automatically each morning, which covers the whole day. Official reply.

sections.heading: Feeding chickens: hay & water
sections.text: Only the interior trough matters. Chickens eat and drink inside before heading out in the morning; with the door open you do not need to fill an outside trough. Official reply.

sections.heading: Feeding chickens: hay & water
sections.text: Top up by hand: hold hay and walk up to an animal to raise its food reserve directly. (Water reserves do not work this way — water comes from troughs.) Single player report, mechanism confirmed in the same official thread.

sections.heading: Feeding chickens: hay & water
sections.text: Getting hay: wild grass produces hay at any growth stage — no need to wait for it to mature. Officially documented (pre-EA update notes; matches current-build behavior reported by players).

sections.heading: Heater, sickness & the vet
sections.text: Quick answer: buy the coop/barn heater and AC from Angela (the chicken seller) — the home-decoration heater and AC sold at City Hall do not work for coops and barns . Mount them on the outside of the coop wall . They prevent temperature sickness but never cure it — a sick animal goes to the vet . Official reply + multiple player reports.

sections.heading: Heater, sickness & the vet
sections.text: Wrong heater is the #1 beginner trap. Support confirmed that many sick-animal reports come from players who installed the house-decoration version. If your chickens keep getting sick with a heater "installed," check which one you bought. Official reply.

sections.heading: Heater, sickness & the vet
sections.text: Placement: the coop/barn unit goes on the exterior wall of the building. Multiple player reports.

sections.heading: Heater, sickness & the vet
sections.text: The vet only treats actual sickness. A famished (starving) animal is turned away — feed it at the coop and it recovers by the next morning. Single player report.

sections.heading: Heater, sickness & the vet
sections.text: Vet fee: unknown. No player has posted a number yet; expect a charge and keep a small reserve.

sections.heading: Heater, sickness & the vet
sections.text: There is no sickness notification in the current build — check your animals manually each day.

sections.heading: Eggs & large eggs
sections.text: Quick answer: once chickens are adult and every need and happiness bar is full , they start laying. Egg size (S/M/L) and fertility are random rolls ; large eggs are the rarest and additionally need the flock to roam in an enclosed outdoor area . Official reply.

sections.heading: Eggs & large eggs
sections.text: Check fertility by hovering over an egg — the tooltip shows whether it is fertile. Official reply.

sections.heading: Eggs & large eggs
sections.text: Large eggs = full needs + enclosed outdoor roaming. An open fence or a missing need blocks them. Official reply.

sections.heading: Eggs & large eggs
sections.text: Pet your chickens daily. Raising their rating noticeably increases large-egg output in player experience; expect several batches before the first large egg. Player reports, direction consistent across sources.

sections.heading: Eggs & large eggs
sections.text: Farming large eggs is the core of the Gigi quest — see the Gigi large-egg quest walkthrough for the full hand-in route.

sections.heading: Automating the coop: silo, water tower, feeder
sections.text: Quick answer: a fully automatic coop needs four pieces working together — an Auto-Feeding Kit on the coop, a Silo loaded with hay, a Water Tower, and a signed water contract — plus the trough set to the right food. If it works, the trough switch shows a green light . Official reply.

sections.heading: Automating the coop: silo, water tower, feeder
sections.text: Install the Auto-Feeding Kit on the coop or barn.

sections.heading: Automating the coop: silo, water tower, feeder
sections.text: Build a Silo within the feeder's range and load it with hay. Hover buildings with the hammer equipped to see what is linked to what.

sections.heading: Automating the coop: silo, water tower, feeder
sections.text: Build a Water Tower — note its link radius is much smaller than the Silo's , so place it closer.

sections.heading: Automating the coop: silo, water tower, feeder
sections.text: Sign the water contract with the Mayor at City Hall first ( map ). Without it the Water Tower never fills; with it, filling is automatic. This is the step most "auto feeder doesn't work" reports are missing. Official reply + player confirmation.

sections.heading: Automating the coop: silo, water tower, feeder
sections.text: Set the trough inside the coop to the correct food/water type and flip the switch — a green light means the setup is live.

sections.heading: Automating the coop: silo, water tower, feeder
sections.text: The Air Conditioning Kit (prevents illness through winter/summer temperature control) follows the same linkage logic. Kit prices and exact ranges are not published; verify placement with the hammer view in your own save. More detail: barn automation in the animal database .

sections.heading: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
sections.text: Still disappearing on 0.8.10.562 or later? Then work this list. Steam normally updates automatically; only check the title-screen version if the problem still occurs.

sections.heading: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
sections.text: Confirm the exact version. A reproduction on 0.8.10.455 or earlier is historical. A 0.8.10.562+ reproduction is useful current evidence.

sections.heading: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
sections.text: Is the coop actually linked? Walk up to the door: the dark panel should show a counter like 0/6 or 3/6 . No counter means the animals are not linked to that coop. Official reply.

sections.heading: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
sections.text: Is the yard fenced? An open gate plus an unfenced entrance area means chickens simply wander off. Multiple player reports.

sections.heading: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
sections.text: Did you install the right heater? Missing (or decoration-version) heating/cooling kills birds to temperature stress. Multiple player reports + official reply.

sections.heading: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
sections.text: Record the transition. Note whether it happened at night entry, growth, birth, loading, subway travel, or a doorway — those are the exact paths named in the official patch.

sections.heading: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
sections.text: Historical workaround, not current advice: before 0.8.10.562, players sometimes recovered a bird stuck at the coop door by moving the other chickens out and demolishing the coop; one report also said a reload restored a vanished bird. Do not demolish a current coop before confirming the new build still reproduces the issue.

sections.heading: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
sections.text: If a bird still vanishes on 0.8.10.562 or later, note the coop counter (x/6), door/fence state, care state and exact transition, then send in your case with the version and screenshots.

sections.heading: Selling animals & making a profit
sections.text: Quick answer: you cannot sell live animals — there is no sale option in the current build. The officially recommended way to cash out spare birds (extra roosters, excess chicks) is to dispatch them and sell the meat . Official reply.

sections.heading: Selling animals & making a profit

parentTitle: The Ranchers Chicken Care Guide: Buying, Feeding, Heaters, Eggs & Profit

title: Feeding chickens: hay & water
parentTitle: The Ranchers Chicken Care Guide: Buying, Feeding, Heaters, Eggs & Profit
description: Quick answer: chickens eat hay . Fill the trough inside the coop — animals eat and drink once automatically each morning, which covers the whole day. Official reply. Only the interior trough matters. Chickens eat and drink inside before heading out in the morning; with the door open you do not need to fill an outside trough. Official reply. Top up by hand: hold hay and walk up to an animal to raise its food reserve directly. (Water reserves do not work this way — water comes from troughs.) Single player report, mechanism confirmed in the same official thread. Getting hay: wild grass produces hay at any growth stage — no need to wait for it to mature. Officially documented (pre-EA update notes; matches current-build behavior reported by players).

title: Heater, sickness & the vet
parentTitle: The Ranchers Chicken Care Guide: Buying, Feeding, Heaters, Eggs & Profit
description: Quick answer: buy the coop/barn heater and AC from Angela (the chicken seller) — the home-decoration heater and AC sold at City Hall do not work for coops and barns . Mount them on the outside of the coop wall . They prevent temperature sickness but never cure it — a sick animal goes to the vet . Official reply + multiple player reports. Wrong heater is the #1 beginner trap. Support confirmed that many sick-animal reports come from players who installed the house-decoration version. If your chickens keep getting sick with a heater "installed," check which one you bought. Official reply. Placement: the coop/barn unit goes on the exterior wall of the building. Multiple player reports. The vet only treats actual sickness. A famished (starving) animal is turned away — feed it at the coop and it recovers by the next morning. Single player report. Vet fee: unknown. No player has posted a number yet; expect a charge and keep a small reserve. There is no sickness notification in the current build — check your animals manually each day.

title: Eggs & large eggs
parentTitle: The Ranchers Chicken Care Guide: Buying, Feeding, Heaters, Eggs & Profit
description: Quick answer: once chickens are adult and every need and happiness bar is full , they start laying. Egg size (S/M/L) and fertility are random rolls ; large eggs are the rarest and additionally need the flock to roam in an enclosed outdoor area . Official reply. Check fertility by hovering over an egg — the tooltip shows whether it is fertile. Official reply. Large eggs = full needs + enclosed outdoor roaming. An open fence or a missing need blocks them. Official reply. Pet your chickens daily. Raising their rating noticeably increases large-egg output in player experience; expect several batches before the first large egg. Player reports, direction consistent across sources. Farming large eggs is the core of the Gigi quest — see the Gigi large-egg quest walkthrough for the full hand-in route.

title: Automating the coop: silo, water tower, feeder
parentTitle: The Ranchers Chicken Care Guide: Buying, Feeding, Heaters, Eggs & Profit
description: Quick answer: a fully automatic coop needs four pieces working together — an Auto-Feeding Kit on the coop, a Silo loaded with hay, a Water Tower, and a signed water contract — plus the trough set to the right food. If it works, the trough switch shows a green light . Official reply. Install the Auto-Feeding Kit on the coop or barn. Build a Silo within the feeder's range and load it with hay. Hover buildings with the hammer equipped to see what is linked to what. Build a Water Tower — note its link radius is much smaller than the Silo's , so place it closer. Sign the water contract with the Mayor at City Hall first ( map ). Without it the Water Tower never fills; with it, filling is automatic. This is the step most "auto feeder doesn't work" reports are missing. Official reply + player confirmation. Set the trough inside the coop to the correct food/water type and flip the switch — a green light means the setup is live. The Air Conditioning Kit (prevents illness through winter/summer temperature control) follows the same linkage logic. Kit prices and exact ranges are not published; verify placement with the hammer view in your own save. More detail: barn automation in the animal database .

title: Chickens disappearing or not eating: the checklist
parentTitle: The Ranchers Chicken Care Guide: Buying, Feeding, Heaters, Eggs & Profit
description: Fixed in 0.8.10.562 · Official Animals disappearing when entering a barn or coop at night. Fixed in 0.8.10.562 · Official Chicks disappearing while progressing to their next growth stage. Fixed in 0.8.10.562 · Official Chicks stuck inside the coop after growing up. Fixed in 0.8.10.562 · Official Newborn mammals failing to appear inside the barn or coop. Fixed in 0.8.10.562 · Official Animals failing to appear after loading a save. Fixed in 0.8.10.562 · Official Animals stuck between a barn/coop and its doors, appearing lost. Fixed in 0.8.10.562 · Official Roped animals freezing after subway travel, or stuck outside the Veterinary Clinic. Still disappearing on 0.8.10.562 or later? Then work this list. Steam normally updates automatically; only check the title-screen version if the problem still occurs. Confirm the exact version. A reproduction on 0.8.10.455 or earlier is historical. A 0.8.10.562+ reproduction is useful current evidence. Is the coop actually linked? Walk up to the door: the dark panel should show a counter like 0/6 or 3/6 . No counter means the animals are not linked to that coop. Official reply. Is the yard fenced? An open gate plus an unfenced entrance area means chickens simply wander off. Multiple player reports. Did you install the right heater? Missing (or decoration-version) heating/cooling kills birds to temperature stress. Multiple player reports + official reply. Record the transition. Note whether it happened at night entry, growth, birth, loading, subway travel, or a doorway — those are the exact paths named in the official patch. Historical workaround, not current advice: before 0.8.10.562, players sometimes recovered a bird stuck at the coop door by moving the other chickens out and demolishing the coop; one report also said a reload restored a vanished bird. Do not demolish a current coop before confirming the new build still reproduces the issue. If a bird still vanishes on 0.8.10.562 or later, note the coop counter (x/6), door/fence state, care state and exact transition, then send in your case with the version and screenshots.

sections.text: Verified against official Steam store copy · Contract terms video-verified August 8, 2026 · Reading time: ~9 min

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: To get power: sign the electricity contract with Victor at City Hall — 1,000C up front, then billed at each day's end by actual consumption. Surplus power you generate is sold back automatically in that same settlement. Solar panel quest stuck? It only counts the ground panel, not the roof one.

sections.heading: What the official material confirms
sections.text: The Steam store page describes ranch management as one of the game's core pillars. Within that pillar, official copy explicitly lists utility management: you can sign water and electricity contracts, or build your own supply with water wells, wind turbines and solar panels. Daily running costs are part of the ranch-management loop alongside crafting, trading and skills.

sections.heading: What the official material confirms
sections.text: The same official description says surplus self-generated energy and water can be sold back to the village, turning utilities from a pure cost into a potential income source.

sections.heading: What the official material confirms
sections.text: What is still not confirmed: the per-unit electricity rate, water contract terms, generation rates, well/turbine/panel output, surplus sale prices, and the exact steps that complete a surplus sale. The contract structure below is video-verified; those figures stay open pending versioned in-game observation.

sections.heading: The electricity contract: quick answer and steps
sections.text: Quick answer: to put your ranch on the grid, sign the electricity contract with Victor, Sunvale's Mayor, at City Hall . You pay a one-time commissioning fee of 1,000C , charged the moment you sign; after that you are billed at the end of each day based on your ranch's actual consumption . If your ranch produces energy, the city can buy your surplus . Contract and surplus sale confirmed by the current Steam store page; terms observed in EA 0.8.10.455.

sections.heading: The electricity contract: quick answer and steps
sections.text: Have at least 1,000C in your bank — that is also the opening requirement of the "Power to the Bench" quest, which walks you through this.

sections.heading: The electricity contract: quick answer and steps
sections.text: Go to City Hall and talk to Victor (the Mayor — show City Hall on the map ). His dialogue also offers a water contract and additional land purchases.

sections.heading: The electricity contract: quick answer and steps
sections.text: Sign the electricity contract. The 1,000C fee is deducted immediately (observed: funds dropped 2,916C → 1,916C on signing).

sections.heading: The electricity contract: quick answer and steps
sections.text: Check each day's settlement screen — consumption is billed there on the Energy line — and watch the Electricity meter app on your phone for per-device usage.

sections.heading: The electricity contract: quick answer and steps
sections.text: Observed billing example: a ranch with one Workbench (5 consumption units) settled one day at Energy −15C Observed in EA 0.8.10.455 . That is a single observation, not a rate table — the per-unit price is not published anywhere we can cite, so do not multiply it out.

sections.heading: The electricity contract: quick answer and steps
sections.text: Water: a water contract option exists in Victor's dialogue, but it was not signed in the observed playthrough — terms stay unknown for now. Self-built supply (water wells, wind turbines, solar panels) is officially confirmed as the alternative route; build costs and daily outputs are still unverified, so record your own numbers before skipping the contract.

sections.text: The smartphone carries an Electricity meter / Water meter app with two tabs Video-observed Games Station, 75:05 . What the Electricity tab showed in the observed playthrough, after the contract was signed:

sections.text: This is the first observed instance of the meter UI structure (device list, per-device consumption, total, efficiency summary). What remains unobserved: the per-unit rate and how generation equipment moves the number positive.

sections.heading: Selling surplus energy
sections.text: Quick answer: you do not sell power to anyone by hand — once you have signed the electricity contract , any surplus your ranch generates is automatically converted in the end-of-day settlement : the Energy line flips from a negative charge to a positive income. If your settlement shows no surplus income, the usual cause is simply that no contract is signed yet. Multiple player reports; contract dialogue confirms the city buys surplus. Observed in EA 0.8.10.455.

sections.heading: Selling surplus energy
sections.text: Reported rates: one player reports buying at 2C per unit and surplus selling back at 1C (buy 3C / sell 1C later in their save). Single-source numbers — they may vary or change with patches.

sections.heading: Selling surplus energy
