title: What the official material confirms
parentTitle: The Ranchers Electricity & Water Guide — Contracts, Power & Selling Surplus
description: The Steam store page describes ranch management as one of the game's core pillars. Within that pillar, official copy explicitly lists utility management: you can sign water and electricity contracts, or build your own supply with water wells, wind turbines and solar panels. Daily running costs are part of the ranch-management loop alongside crafting, trading and skills. The same official description says surplus self-generated energy and water can be sold back to the village, turning utilities from a pure cost into a potential income source. What is still not confirmed: the per-unit electricity rate, water contract terms, generation rates, well/turbine/panel output, surplus sale prices, and the exact steps that complete a surplus sale. The contract structure below is video-verified; those figures stay open pending versioned in-game observation.

title: The electricity contract: quick answer and steps
parentTitle: The Ranchers Electricity & Water Guide — Contracts, Power & Selling Surplus
description: Quick answer: to put your ranch on the grid, sign the electricity contract with Victor, Sunvale's Mayor, at City Hall . You pay a one-time commissioning fee of 1,000C , charged the moment you sign; after that you are billed at the end of each day based on your ranch's actual consumption . If your ranch produces energy, the city can buy your surplus . Contract and surplus sale confirmed by the current Steam store page; terms observed in EA 0.8.10.455. Have at least 1,000C in your bank — that is also the opening requirement of the "Power to the Bench" quest, which walks you through this. Go to City Hall and talk to Victor (the Mayor — show City Hall on the map ). His dialogue also offers a water contract and additional land purchases. Sign the electricity contract. The 1,000C fee is deducted immediately (observed: funds dropped 2,916C → 1,916C on signing). Check each day's settlement screen — consumption is billed there on the Energy line — and watch the Electricity meter app on your phone for per-device usage. Observed billing example: a ranch with one Workbench (5 consumption units) settled one day at Energy −15C Observed in EA 0.8.10.455 . That is a single observation, not a rate table — the per-unit price is not published anywhere we can cite, so do not multiply it out. Water: a water contract option exists in Victor's dialogue, but it was not signed in the observed playthrough — terms stay unknown for now. Self-built supply (water wells, wind turbines, solar panels) is officially confirmed as the alternative route; build costs and daily outputs are still unverified, so record your own numbers before skipping the contract.

title: The meter interface (video-observed)
parentTitle: The Ranchers Electricity & Water Guide — Contracts, Power & Selling Surplus
description: The smartphone carries an Electricity meter / Water meter app with two tabs Video-observed Games Station, 75:05 . What the Electricity tab showed in the observed playthrough, after the contract was signed: Electricity contract status: Contract Active — the contract state is visible in the meter UI, not only in the quest log. Device list: Workbench ×1, consuming 5 units, with an efficiency value of 0; total consumption shown as 5. "Your ranch's energy efficiency: −5" — a worked example of a deficit state: with no generation built, the ranch ran at −5, matching the official claim that daily running costs are part of the loop. title: Selling surplus energy
parentTitle: The Ranchers Electricity & Water Guide — Contracts, Power & Selling Surplus
description: Quick answer: you do not sell power to anyone by hand — once you have signed the electricity contract , any surplus your ranch generates is automatically converted in the end-of-day settlement : the Energy line flips from a negative charge to a positive income. If your settlement shows no surplus income, the usual cause is simply that no contract is signed yet. Multiple player reports; contract dialogue confirms the city buys surplus. Observed in EA 0.8.10.455. Reported rates: one player reports buying at 2C per unit and surplus selling back at 1C (buy 3C / sell 1C later in their save). Single-source numbers — they may vary or change with patches. One unresolved case: a player reports a +5 surplus day that still charged 33C — possibly a threshold or a bug; the community has no conclusion yet. If this hits you, record the meter and settlement screens and report it. Water surplus follows the same officially advertised idea, but the water contract was not signed in the observed playthrough, so water-sale behavior stays unknown.

sections.heading: What official material confirms
sections.text: Official Kickstarter and store material describe a construction system built around freedom: you build your dream house both inside and out, with friends able to feel at home in the structures you design. The same source names more than 200 building items spanning foundations, windows, ceilings and other components.

sections.heading: What official material confirms
sections.text: The game runs on RedPilz Studio's in-house Systemic Engine. Official copy says every prop is interactable and reacts to weather and to classical elements such as water, fire and air. That claim is about behavior, not about placement rules.

sections.heading: What official material confirms
sections.text: Broader ranch construction is also confirmed in the official feature overview: house construction, animal facilities, fences, sprinklers, greenhouses and utility systems are all named as buildable ranch infrastructure.

sections.heading: What official material confirms
sections.text: What is not confirmed: whether placement uses a grid, which specific part satisfies each objective, and how the parts system behaves when an objective fails. None of that is published in the official material we can cite, so this guide keeps it as TBD pending a versioned in-game observation .

sections.heading: What official material confirms
sections.text: Official Accidental demolition refunds half the materials. The pre-EA Ranching v2 update notes state that all crafted buildings give 50% of their resources back when destroyed accidentally — a quality-of-life safety net, not a free redesign: you still lose the other half, so demolish deliberately. This is pre-EA official documentation ; the exact refund behavior has not yet been independently rechecked in the current EA build.

title: What official material confirms
parentTitle: The Ranchers Building & Placement Guide — Construction, Parts & Placement Issues
description: Official Kickstarter and store material describe a construction system built around freedom: you build your dream house both inside and out, with friends able to feel at home in the structures you design. The same source names more than 200 building items spanning foundations, windows, ceilings and other components. The game runs on RedPilz Studio's in-house Systemic Engine. Official copy says every prop is interactable and reacts to weather and to classical elements such as water, fire and air. That claim is about behavior, not about placement rules. Broader ranch construction is also confirmed in the official feature overview: house construction, animal facilities, fences, sprinklers, greenhouses and utility systems are all named as buildable ranch infrastructure. What is not confirmed: whether placement uses a grid, which specific part satisfies each objective, and how the parts system behaves when an objective fails. None of that is published in the official material we can cite, so this guide keeps it as TBD pending a versioned in-game observation . Official Accidental demolition refunds half the materials. The pre-EA Ranching v2 update notes state that all crafted buildings give 50% of their resources back when destroyed accidentally — a quality-of-life safety net, not a free redesign: you still lose the other half, so demolish deliberately. This is pre-EA official documentation ; the exact refund behavior has not yet been independently rechecked in the current EA build.

title: Workbench crafting menu (video-observed)
parentTitle: The Ranchers Building & Placement Guide — Construction, Parts & Placement Issues
description: The workbench crafting menu was read on screen in launch-build footage (Games Station, V0.8.10.455) Video-observed at 70:50–71:40 . The menu is organized into four tabs: Others / Farming / Shelters / Furniture . Recipes visible on screen: 8 Stone + 10 Wood Log Requirements not yet captured Video-observed (listing only) Scarecrow / Bob the Scarecrow Basic Sprinkler / Advanced Sprinkler / Green House Sprinkler Concrete foundation / Rocks foundation / Wood foundation Rope · Torch · FlashLight · Small Manual Bomb · Fire extinguisher · Workbench Only the Red Tent recipe was opened on screen, so the material counts for every other row stay unrecorded rather than guessed. The three sprinkler tiers and the Water Well confirm the utility-infrastructure build path named in official copy, and the scarecrow recipes connect to the Feathered Foes quest described in the beginner's guide . Official Bulk crafting is supported both at workbenches and in the Craft App, per the official community-update notes (pre-EA); recheck against the current EA build.

title: Materials: Stone, Wood, Hay, Charcoal and Zirconite
parentTitle: The Ranchers Building & Placement Guide — Construction, Parts & Placement Issues
description: Quick answer: use the materials database for the current source and evidence boundary of each material. Stone: collect the loose supply on land you own first. A reliable repeatable route after that supply is exhausted is still being verified. Wood Logs: current community reports obtain them from trees; exact respawn and ownership rules remain unverified. Hay: confirmed chicken feed, but the public gathering route is still based on a single current-build report. Charcoal: multiple current players burn Wood Logs and use a fire extinguisher before collecting the result. The retained evidence does not lock down one key binding or exact timer. title: Parts, objectives and the building loop
parentTitle: The Ranchers Building & Placement Guide — Construction, Parts & Placement Issues
description: Official copy confirms the parts catalogue and the objective-driven tutorial, but not the exact rules connecting them. The practical consequence for a new rancher is simple: do not assume a part counts toward an objective until the current build confirms it. Parts catalogue: more than 200 building items including foundations, windows, ceilings and structural components. Objectives: construction quests ask for specific results (for example, a roof or a set of exterior walls). Which pieces count is decided by the live build, not by the part's name alone. Placement freedom: the intended system is flexible design; the current build's placement and undo behavior is what actually matters when a piece misbehaves. Grid behavior: not officially confirmed. Until a current-build test records whether pieces snap to a grid, treat free-form and grid placement both as unverified. The official store copy also lists construction among the first-week tutorial topics, so the main quest is the best place to learn what your build actually accepts.

title: What to record before placing
parentTitle: The Ranchers Building & Placement Guide — Construction, Parts & Placement Issues
description: If you hit a placement problem, the evidence this site needs is a dated, versioned record of the objective and the exact pieces used. Exact quest text: the objective's wording, not a paraphrase, including the requested count. Blueprint names: the specific pieces placed, in order, and which were rejected. Parcel state: whether the building site or parcel was purchased and its ownership state. Build number: every record must name the version, because Early Access changes frequently. Two independent current-build records under comparable conditions promote a finding to Corroborated . Until then, a single report is a useful test lead, not a settled fact.

title: Roof Quest Stuck in The Ranchers? Building Quest Fixes That Work
description: The Ranchers roof quest not completing? The quest tracker getting stuck is an officially confirmed known issue. Try the phone quest journal (T), sleep to the next day, or restart — plus fixes for missing roof and door blueprints at the workbench.

sections.heading: Roof Quest Stuck in The Ranchers? Building Quest Fixes That Work
sections.text: Updated for Early Access 0.8.10.x (August 2026) · August 7, 2026 · Reading time: ~7 min

sections.heading: Roof Quest Stuck in The Ranchers? Building Quest Fixes That Work
sections.text: If your roof quest will not complete after you built the roof, you are not alone — this was one of the most-reported problems on the Steam discussion board in the first week of August 2026, with players posting about it in English, German and Russian, and some getting stuck even earlier at the first step of placing stairs ( Tutorial build roof , Aug 4; Whitebear, Aug 2; Campingqueen769, Aug 3).

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: The quest tracker getting stuck is an officially confirmed known issue Official . Do these three things in order:

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Press T and check the quest journal on your phone — the next objective may already be listed there even though the on-screen tracker looks stuck, and you can keep playing.

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Sleep to the next day.

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Restart the game client (save first, then fully quit and relaunch).

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: If the real problem is that you cannot find the roof, door or bed blueprints at the workbench, that is a different issue — a scrolling UI quirk — covered in Symptom B below.

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Symptom A: roof built, quest will not complete

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Symptom B: no roof, door or bed blueprint at the workbench

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Symptom C: cannot build a door

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Symptom D: hole in the middle of the roof

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Troubleshooting flow

sections.heading: Symptom A: roof built, quest will not complete (tracker stuck)
sections.text: Official Corroborated by players

sections.heading: Symptom A: roof built, quest will not complete (tracker stuck)
sections.text: This is the officially confirmed case. Moderator/support Jennoula confirmed in "Tutorial build roof" (Aug 4, 2026) that "there is a known issue with the quest tracker sometimes getting stuck," and gave the workarounds that have worked for almost every player so far:

sections.heading: Symptom A: roof built, quest will not complete (tracker stuck)
sections.text: Press T and see whether your next objective shows up in the phone quest journal. The on-screen tracker may still look stuck, but you can continue the quest anyway.

sections.heading: Symptom A: roof built, quest will not complete (tracker stuck)
sections.text: Sleep to the next day — this sometimes gets the tracker moving again.

sections.heading: Symptom A: roof built, quest will not complete (tracker stuck)
sections.text: Restart the game client.

sections.heading: Symptom A: roof built, quest will not complete (tracker stuck)
sections.text: The developers are still investigating why the tracker gets stuck, but you should be able to continue in the meantime.

sections.heading: Symptom A: roof built, quest will not complete (tracker stuck)
sections.text: Two independent players corroborate the restart/logout route in "Cant finish Roof quest...?" (Aug 3): X-C0brA-X saved, restarted the game, and the quest showed as finished after the restart; KnottyBoy did the quest steps via the phone journal, then logged totally out and back in, after which the on-screen quest passed.

sections.heading: Symptom B: no roof, door or bed blueprint at the workbench (UI scrolling)
sections.text: Corroborated by players

sections.heading: Symptom B: no roof, door or bed blueprint at the workbench (UI scrolling)
sections.text: Before assuming your game is broken, check how far you scrolled. In "Missing roof" (Aug 2), SUwUMaBUwU pointed out that roofs and beds sit far to the right in the building tab list — scroll slowly with the mouse wheel, because scrolling too far flips you over to the furniture tab. Minay, who had restarted and even started a new save without success, confirmed that scrolling slowly with the mouse wheel revealed the roofs and beds.

sections.heading: Symptom B: no roof, door or bed blueprint at the workbench (UI scrolling)
sections.text: A second, independent group reported the same class of problem for door blueprints in "No door plan at workbench" (Aug 4): rllewis3 found that workbench pages can be dragged back and forth with the left mouse button, which revealed plans that seemed missing; jw62157 (the thread author) realized that clicking the arrow keys at the top slides the choices over but often hides some blueprints behind the left panel that keeps opening.

sections.heading: Symptom B: no roof, door or bed blueprint at the workbench (UI scrolling)
sections.text: Practical takeaway: use slow mouse-wheel scrolling or left-mouse dragging to page the workbench list, and be careful with the top arrow buttons — they can leave blueprints hidden behind the side panel.

sections.heading: Symptom C: cannot build a door
sections.text: One player, Earth Hunter (in "No door plan at workbench" , Aug 4), reports that the blueprint list contains two door types — an exterior door and an interior door — and that you also need a wall with a door opening for the door to fit. This is a single community report, not officially confirmed, but it matches the building system's wall-cutout logic and is worth checking before reporting a bug.

sections.heading: Symptom D: hole in the middle of the roof (Roof Cap Lvl 2)
sections.text: Single report unverified

sections.heading: Symptom D: hole in the middle of the roof (Roof Cap Lvl 2)
sections.text: Several players use Roof Cap Lvl 2 to fill the hole in the middle and then wonder whether that counts. One player, bucfanjoe (in "Cant finish Roof quest...?" , Aug 3), reports that their own build moved past the roof step even with a hole in the middle, as long as the exterior edges had a roof tile — but notes being unsure whether Lvl 2 caps count, and adds that having actual doors and windows placed in the wall cutouts may matter. Treat this as a single unverified report: if Symptom A's fixes fail, completing the

sections.heading: Troubleshooting flow (our consolidated checklist)
sections.text: Work through these in order — each step rules out one of the symptoms above:

sections.heading: Troubleshooting flow (our consolidated checklist)
sections.text: Can you find the blueprint at all? If no roof/door/bed plan appears at the workbench, fix the UI first: slow mouse-wheel scroll, left-mouse drag, avoid the top arrows hiding plans behind the side panel ( Symptom B ).

sections.heading: Troubleshooting flow (our consolidated checklist)
sections.text: Is the building actually complete? Walls placed, wall with a door opening for the door, exterior and interior door types distinguished ( Symptom C ), roof tiles on all exterior edges ( Symptom D ).

sections.heading: Troubleshooting flow (our consolidated checklist)
sections.text: Is the tracker stuck? Building done but the quest will not advance → press T and check the phone quest journal, sleep to the next day, then restart the client ( Symptom A , officially confirmed known issue).

sections.heading: Troubleshooting flow (our consolidated checklist)
sections.text: Still stuck after all three? Report it on the Steam discussion board with your build version and screenshots — the developers are actively investigating the tracker issue.

sections.heading: Roof quest FAQ
sections.text: I built the roof exactly as shown. Why won't the quest complete?

sections.heading: Roof quest FAQ
sections.text: Most likely the quest tracker is stuck — an officially confirmed known issue in Early Access. Press T to check the phone quest journal (the next step may already be there), sleep to the next day, or restart the client. These workarounds have worked for almost every player so far, per the support team.

sections.heading: Roof quest FAQ
sections.text: There are no roof or bed blueprints in my workbench. Is my save broken?

sections.heading: Roof quest FAQ
sections.text: Probably not. Multiple players "missing" roofs, beds and doors were actually hitting a scrolling UI quirk: the plans sit far right in the building tab, fast scrolling overshoots into the furniture tab, and the top arrow buttons can hide plans behind the left panel. Scroll slowly with the mouse wheel or drag the pages with the left mouse button.

sections.heading: Roof quest FAQ
sections.text: Does a Roof Cap Lvl 2 hole in the middle block the quest?

sections.heading: Roof quest FAQ
sections.text: Unknown. One player reports progressing with a hole in the middle as long as exterior edges had roof tiles, but was unsure whether Lvl 2 caps count — a single unverified report. If the official tracker fixes fail, edging the roof and fitting doors/windows into wall cutouts is a sensible next test.

title: Troubleshooting flow (our consolidated checklist)
parentTitle: Roof Quest Stuck in The Ranchers? Building Quest Fixes That Work
description: Work through these in order — each step rules out one of the symptoms above: Can you find the blueprint at all? If no roof/door/bed plan appears at the workbench, fix the UI first: slow mouse-wheel scroll, left-mouse drag, avoid the top arrows hiding plans behind the side panel ( Symptom B ). Is the building actually complete? Walls placed, wall with a door opening for the door, exterior and interior door types distinguished ( Symptom C ), roof tiles on all exterior edges ( Symptom D ). Is the tracker stuck? Building done but the quest will not advance → press T and check the phone quest journal, sleep to the next day, then restart the client ( Symptom A , officially confirmed known issue). Still stuck after all three? Report it on the Steam discussion board with your build version and screenshots — the developers are actively investigating the tracker issue.

title: Roof quest FAQ
parentTitle: Roof Quest Stuck in The Ranchers? Building Quest Fixes That Work
description: I built the roof exactly as shown. Why won't the quest complete? Most likely the quest tracker is stuck — an officially confirmed known issue in Early Access. Press T to check the phone quest journal (the next step may already be there), sleep to the next day, or restart the client. These workarounds have worked for almost every player so far, per the support team. There are no roof or bed blueprints in my workbench. Is my save broken? Probably not. Multiple players "missing" roofs, beds and doors were actually hitting a scrolling UI quirk: the plans sit far right in the building tab, fast scrolling overshoots into the furniture tab, and the top arrow buttons can hide plans behind the left panel. Scroll slowly with the mouse wheel or drag the pages with the left mouse button. Does a Roof Cap Lvl 2 hole in the middle block the quest? Unknown. One player reports progressing with a hole in the middle as long as exterior edges had roof tiles, but was unsure whether Lvl 2 caps count — a single unverified report. If the official tracker fixes fail, edging the roof and fitting doors/windows into wall cutouts is a sensible next test.

title: Real Eggs, Real Evidence: Gigi Quest Walkthrough (The Ranchers)
description: The Ranchers Gigi quest walkthrough: get 2 large eggs by raising chicken ratings, take the subway (not a car) for the police chase, follow the mini-map star to her house, and what to do when Gigi keeps following you or the quest disappears.

sections.heading: Real Eggs, Real Evidence: Gigi Quest Walkthrough (The Ranchers)
sections.text: Updated for Early Access 0.8.10.562 · August 11, 2026 · Reading time: ~8 min

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: One-sentence version of the quest: pet your chickens daily until their rating rises and they lay 2 large eggs, manually save, then take the subway — not a car — to hand the eggs over, escape the police on foot, and follow the mini-map star marker all the way to Gigi's front door to finish.

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: The two most common failure points: players never get large eggs because they do not raise the chickens' rating ( step 1 ), and the final hand-in bugs out if you drive or if Gigi will not leave your car ( step 4 ). Yes, the quest is completable in Early Access — and no, Gigi not contacting you afterwards matches what other players see — multiple players report no further quest has appeared in the current build ( details ).

sections.heading: Step 1: getting 2 large eggs
sections.text: The quest needs 2 large eggs , and regular eggs do not count — Bobthekiller's exact blocker in "Real eggs, real evidence" (Aug 4, 2026) was only ever receiving regular eggs. DJM's answer in the same thread: pet the chickens every day; when their rating goes up, they start laying larger eggs , and once you have 2, the quest shows you where to take them. So if you never see large eggs, the fix is daily petting to raise the rating, not more hens.

sections.heading: Egg fertility and the "Infertile" label
sections.text: Hotfix 0.8.10.562 also replaced the egg label "Failed to hatch" with "Infertile" for clarity — an official confirmation that a fertility/hatching mechanic exists in the current build. We have not re-tested hatching details (rates, incubation conditions) on 0.8.10.562, so nothing beyond the label change is claimed here. For the quest itself only large-egg drops matter; fertility is relevant only if you are trying to hatch chicks from eggs.

sections.heading: Step 2–3: handing over the eggs and escaping the police
sections.text: Handing over the eggs triggers a police chase, and three independent players give the same advice: take the subway to the hand-in, do not drive (Seansniper27 — "went in by subway and not car, found out the hard way"; bucfanjoe; Fight or Flight Gamer). A car chase with the starter vehicle is where most failed attempts happen.

sections.heading: Step 2–3: handing over the eggs and escaping the police
sections.text: For escaping on foot, bucfanjoe describes a route that worked ( "Large Egg Quest Gone" , Aug 3): run for the river — it usually shakes the drones — then continue under the ferris wheel and up toward the museum until the police lose you, then let Gigi catch up. Seansniper27 adds that the next objective can point you to her house, back to the hand-in spot, or somewhere in between — watch the tracker rather than assuming one fixed destination.

WildW0lf, whose car was impounded mid-quest, could never get Gigi back into a car and had to abandon the quest.

Following the mini-map star on foot, with Gigi following, led to her house — and only once at her front door did she become available to talk to, which cleared the quest. sections.heading: If the quest disappears after failing
sections.text: Reports conflict here. AlterEgoGenral believes a failed quest can simply be retaken, but aes1218 ( "Large Egg Quest Gone" , Aug 3) failed the escape twice and reports the quest disappearing entirely, with no found way to re-trigger it. Whether a failed Gigi quest can always be re-accepted is currently Unknown. Our site recommendation: make a manual save before handing over the eggs , so a failed escape costs you a reload instead of the quest line. See our failed-quest replay page for the general recovery route.

sections.heading: Gigi quest FAQ
sections.text: Large eggs are tied to your chickens' rating, not luck or coop count. Pet the chickens every day; once the rating rises, they start laying large eggs, and with 2 in hand the quest shows the delivery point.

sections.heading: Gigi quest FAQ
sections.text: Gigi keeps following me and won't get out / won't go home. What do I do?

sections.heading: Gigi quest FAQ
sections.text: Check the mini-map for a mission star marker — it can appear there while staying absent from the big map. Walk (do not drive) to that star, which is her house; she only becomes interactable at her front door. Reloads do not reliably fix this state for everyone, so the subway + on-foot route is the prevention.

sections.text: Gigi said she'd contact me but never did. Is my quest line bugged?

sections.heading: Gigi quest FAQ
sections.text: Probably not. Multiple players report that no further quest has appeared after "Real Eggs, Real Evidence" in the current Early Access build — players waited into Summer and Autumn with no follow-up. We treat the line as ending here unless official notes or new reports show otherwise.

sections.heading: Police Wanted Levels in The Ranchers: Codes, Force and Surrender Rules
sections.text: Official pre-EA design reviewed against Early Access 0.8.10.x · August 9, 2026 · Reading time: ~5 min

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Official pre-EA design The Police District Update describes a 5-level wanted system , escalating from peaceful fine collection to heavy lethal weapons. It also describes surrender as a way to reduce sentence and bail. The current 0.8.10.x surrender prompt, key and trigger have not been independently rechecked , so this page separates documented design from current-build observations.

sections.heading: The 5 wanted levels, level by level
sections.text: Police drones aim for a peaceful resolution — they will not arrest or attack if you pay your fines. This level handles minor offenses.

sections.heading: The 5 wanted levels, level by level
sections.text: Pay up and you avoid custody entirely; carry on with your day.

sections.heading: The 5 wanted levels, level by level
sections.text: No lethal force, but the police strongly encourage you to surrender.

sections.text: If caught — or if you surrender — you are taken into police custody, likely with a sentence.

sections.text: Police drones switch to non-lethal, dissuasive tactics.

sections.heading: The 5 wanted levels, level by level
sections.text: Getting caught means custody with a probable sentence.

sections.heading: The 5 wanted levels, level by level
sections.text: Police are now authorized to use light lethal weapons ; their goal is to end the chase quickly.

sections.heading: The 5 wanted levels, level by level
sections.text: Custody on capture — now under live fire.

sections.heading: The 5 wanted levels, level by level
sections.text: Heavy lethal weapons are in play to end the chase at all costs; the police will do whatever it takes.

sections.heading: The 5 wanted levels, level by level
sections.text: The highest-force response in the game — surrender is the cheap way out.

sections.heading: Surrender vs. getting caught
sections.text: Official pre-EA design The announcement says that at any wanted level you can surrender for a lower sentence and bail, or keep trying to evade. If you surrender or are caught, it describes custody, fines and possible jail time. This confirms the intended option, not the current input: the site does not yet have a current-build screenshot showing the surrender prompt or key.

sections.heading: Surrender vs. getting caught
sections.text: One multiplayer silver lining from the same announcement: while you are in custody, your friends can join your game, visit you, and take care of your crops and cattle.

sections.heading: Evasion: how the search ends
sections.text: Official Losing the pursuers is not instantly over: police cars continue searching for you briefly . If they catch you again during that window, the chase restarts. If you manage to stay hidden for a while, you are eventually considered evaded — and a successful evasion wipes your fines and lets you keep all your loot .

sections.heading: Evasion: how the search ends
sections.text: So the risk/reward trade at high wanted levels is explicit: surrender early for reduced fines and bail, or gamble on hiding through the short search window for a clean slate.

sections.heading: Wanted level FAQ
sections.text: Can I just pay my way out of a wanted level?

sections.heading: Wanted level FAQ
sections.text: At Level 1, yes — paying the fine resolves it peacefully with no custody. From Level 2 upward, surrender or capture means custody, a cell, fines and possibly jail days; surrendering still reduces the sentence and bail compared with being caught.

sections.heading: Wanted level FAQ
sections.text: When do the police start using lethal force?

sections.heading: Wanted level FAQ
sections.text: Level 4 (Code Red) authorizes light lethal weapons and Level 5 (Code Black) brings heavy lethal weapons. Levels 1–3 are non-lethal: fine collection at Level 1, surrender pressure at Level 2, and non-lethal dissuasive tactics at Level 3.

sections.heading: Wanted level FAQ
sections.text: I lost the cops — why are police cars still after me?

sections.heading: Wanted level FAQ
sections.text: That is the official search behavior: police cars keep searching briefly after you break the chase, and being spotted restarts it. Stay hidden through that window and you are considered evaded — fines wiped, loot kept.

sections.heading: Wanted level FAQ
sections.text: Is surrendering ever worth it at Level 5?

sections.heading: Wanted level FAQ
sections.text: Per the official notes, surrendering at any wanted level — including Level 5 — leads to lesser fines and fewer jail days than being caught, while a successful evasion wipes fines entirely. The choice is reduced penalty versus all-or-nothing escape under heavy lethal force.

title: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: The Ranchers farming guide with labeled evidence for empty-plot watering, harvest timing, reported season-change crop loss, strawberry and lettuce regrow behavior, CashIn selling and the fertilizer warning pending a current-build retest.

sections.heading: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
sections.text: Page baseline: current official version 0.8.10.562 (August 2026) · Video observations recorded on build 0.8.10.455 · August 11, 2026 · Reading time: ~8 min

sections.heading: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
sections.text: Farming questions — how do I start a field, do I have to water every day, what happens if I forget to harvest — fill the Steam discussion board, but most answers there mix Alpha-era memory with the current Early Access build. This page only prints what our evidence log actually supports, and puts the two biggest unknowns (tilling and greenhouses) in a clearly marked "not yet verified" section instead of guessing.

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Empty tilled plots need attention if you want to keep them. Player reports say an empty, unseeded plot reverts after roughly three dry days; rain counts as water. The watering interval for a planted crop is still unverified Corroborated for empty plots .

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Forgetting to harvest does not destroy your crop. Fruit and vegetables stay on the plant; seeds are only lost when the plant itself dies Official pre-EA update, not yet re-tested on 0.8.10.562 .

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Players report seasonal crops disappearing at a season change. One reply identifies day 30 as the last harvest day and day 1 as the rollover; treat that exact cutoff as a reported rule until it is reproduced Current-build reports .

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Sell through the CashIn chest — full workflow in the money-making guide .

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: Avoid a large fertilizer investment for now. Support officially warned that its calculation was incorrect; 0.8.10.562 did not announce a fix, and current behavior has not been re-tested here Official warning .

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: How to open a new field, and how to unlock the greenhouse, are not yet verified — see the hold section before trusting any older tutorial.

sections.heading: Forgetting to harvest & when seeds disappear
sections.text: Official pre-Early-Access update (Dec 2, 2025), mechanism assumed live but not yet re-tested on 0.8.10.562

sections.heading: Forgetting to harvest & when seeds disappear
sections.text: The developers' last pre-launch mechanics update, "Bigger, better and truly next level!" (Dec 2, 2025), states the new plantation rules directly:

sections.heading: Forgetting to harvest & when seeds disappear
sections.text: Seeds only disappear when the plant dies. A planted seed is not consumed by harvesting or by time alone.

sections.heading: Forgetting to harvest & when seeds disappear
sections.text: Fruits and vegetables no longer get destroyed if you forget to harvest them. Ripe produce waits on the plant instead of rotting away.

sections.heading: Forgetting to harvest & when seeds disappear
sections.text: A simpler, more intuitive re-grow flow for recurring crops.

sections.heading: Forgetting to harvest & when seeds disappear
sections.text: Because this wording comes from an official update and no later patch note (through 0.8.10.562) contradicts it, we treat these as the working rules — with the explicit caveat that they were announced before Early Access launch and we have not yet re-verified each line in-game on the current build.

sections.heading: Season-change crop loss: current reports, exact cutoff unverified
sections.text: Current-build reports

sections.heading: Season-change crop loss: current reports, exact cutoff unverified
sections.text: Two current-build threads report crops disappearing around a season boundary, but they do not independently establish every calendar detail. In "WTF ?? A whole field of eggplants gone after sleeping ???" (Aug 3, 2026), the poster lost an entire eggplant field overnight; player Mancer explained that day 30 is the last harvest day, day 1 begins the new season, and seasonal crops are removed during the rollover. FIDELIS reported disappearing eggplants in "Things disappear" (Aug 6), but that report alone does not verif

sections.heading: Season-change crop loss: current reports, exact cutoff unverified
sections.text: Mancer's season-seed list from the same thread is a single community report, so treat it as a working reference, not gospel: summer — green lettuce, eggplant, corn; spring — strawberries, garlic, green salad; autumn — onions, carrots, pumpkins. Our own video-observed data confirms strawberry as a spring seed and red lettuce with a spring tag on build 0.8.10.455 (see the crop database ).

sections.heading: Season-change crop loss: current reports, exact cutoff unverified
sections.text: Practical takeaway: check the calendar before a big planting run late in a season — seeds planted on day 28 of a season may never reach their first harvest.

sections.heading: Regrow vs one-time crops
sections.text: Video-observed recorded on build 0.8.10.455

sections.heading: Regrow vs one-time crops
sections.text: Retained gameplay footage of the launch build shows the two crop archetypes side by side:

sections.heading: Regrow vs one-time crops
sections.text: Strawberry Seeds (144C): spring seed, first harvest 7 days after planting, then re-harvests every 3 days — a recurring crop.

sections.heading: Regrow vs one-time crops
sections.text: Red Lettuce Seeds (48C): spring seed, matures in 3 days with no regrow line on the seed description — a one-time crop you replant.

sections.heading: Regrow vs one-time crops
sections.text: The official pre-EA update's "simpler re-grow flow for recurring crops" Official matches this split: recurring crops keep their plant and cycle again, one-time crops are replanted from new seeds. Exact regrow intervals for other crops are still being collected — the crop database tracks each one with its own evidence label.

sections.heading: Watering: what is known and what is not
sections.text: Empty plots corroborated Tools official pre-EA update

sections.heading: Watering: what is known and what is not
sections.text: Two independent discussion threads answer why empty tilled plots disappear. In "Agricultural fields?!" (Jul 31, 2026), players say unwatered, unseeded plots vanish after a few days; in "Removing Farming Patches?" (Jul 31), another player estimates about 3 days without rain, watering or crops/weeds and says rain counts. These reports do not establish how often a planted crop must be watered, so this page no longer turns the empty-plot timer into crop-care advice.

sections.heading: Watering: what is known and what is not
sections.text: The same Dec 2, 2025 official update also confirms the watering toolset exists and was tuned: sprinkler timings adjusted to water plantations more quickly , and a larger area of effect for the watering can Official pre-EA . Launch-build footage shows three sprinkler tiers and a water well in the crafting menu's farming tab Video-observed build 0.8.10.455 . One German-language player report mentions a watering can covering about 7 fields and an advanced sprinkler covering 25 — a Single report we have not corroborate

sections.heading: Watering: what is known and what is not
sections.text: What we do not know yet: how a sprinkler connects to water or power (pipe, cable, well radius or none) is not shown in any retained source, so we deliberately do not print hookup instructions. Treat sprinkler placement as finicky too — one player calls placement "still wonky" ( same thread , single report).

sections.heading: Selling your harvest
sections.text: Harvests are sold through the CashIn chest : deposit produce during the day and the money lands as the "Farming" line of the end-of-day settlement, which does not break down per crop. The full observed workflow — linking the chest, depositing, and reading the bill — is documented step by step in the money-making guide's CashIn section , so we do not repeat it here.

sections.heading: Selling your harvest
sections.text: The Dec 2, 2025 update also mentions an economy pass with fruit, vegetable and seed prices adjusted Official pre-EA , which is why we never quote Alpha-era price lists as current values. Per-crop sell prices remain unknown while the settlement screen stays aggregated — see the crop database for what is measured versus pending.

sections.heading: Fertilizer: official warning, current behavior pending
sections.text: Official warning issued Aug 4, 2026; 0.8.10.562 behavior not re-tested

sections.heading: Fertilizer: official warning, current behavior pending
sections.text: In "Furtilizer not worth it" (Aug 3, 2026), a player documented spending 8,000C on legendary fertilizer that covered 8 of 24 plots and netted only 79C of extra profit. Support moderator Jennoula replied on Aug 4, 2026: "we are aware that the fertilizer is not currently calculating correctly and it is being looked into, so for now just avoid investing in fertilizer until we get it adjusted again."

sections.heading: Fertilizer: official warning, current behavior pending
sections.text: The 0.8.10.562 hotfix notes (Aug 10, 2026) do not announce a fertilizer fix , but omission from patch notes is not proof that behavior stayed unchanged. We have not re-tested fertilizer on 0.8.10.562. Until a current-build test or official reply confirms the calculation was adjusted, the cautious recommendation is to avoid a large fertilizer investment . Fertilizer is still visible in the shop (Leafy Market's Seed & Fertilizer tab, video-observed on 0.8.10.455) — availability does not verify its return.

sections.heading: Not yet verified: tilling & greenhouses
sections.text: These two topics decide how you start and extend a farm, but our evidence for the current build is not strong enough to print instructions. Rather than copying 2022 Alpha tutorials, we hold both:

sections.heading: How do you open a new field? (Hold)
sections.text: Historical Unverified lead

sections.heading: How do you open a new field? (Hold)
sections.text: The only hoe-based tilling account on record is from the 2022 Alpha (a player buying seeds and a hoe, planting and watering daily) — useful as a hint that a hoe tool is involved, but two major versions out of date. Current-build evidence only proves the mechanic is called "tilling" and that tilled plots revert to normal ground on their own (a feedback thread asks for a way to undo tilling, Aug 6, 2026; the dry-out threads above). Launch-build footage shows three "foundation"-type items in the crafting menu's farmin

sections.heading: How do you open a new field? (Hold)
sections.text: Planned verification (not yet done): buy the hoe at the seed shop, use it on open ground, record the exact prompts and whether a plot appears; then place each of the three farming-tab "foundation" items and document what they create. Until that is recorded, any step-by-step "how to till" you read elsewhere — including anything we could write — is unverified.

sections.text: Historical Single report

sections.heading: What is the greenhouse and how do you unlock it? (Hold)
sections.text: The greenhouse appears in official materials as one of the ways to build out the farm, and one current-build player (Mancer, in the eggplant thread ) reports that greenhouses allow out-of-season planting , saying they tested planting in winter with one — a single self-reported test, not yet corroborated. The only unlock-path evidence on record is from November 2022 : the developers confirmed back then that the greenhouse blueprint was sold by Lina and required both materials and money. Whether that vendor, price an

sections.heading: What is the greenhouse and how do you unlock it? (Hold)
sections.text: Planned verification (not yet done): check Lina's blueprint list on the current build for a greenhouse entry and its material cost; if built, test an out-of-season seed inside and record the result.

sections.heading: Known limitations
sections.text: The harvest, seed-loss and regrow rules come from the official Dec 2, 2025 pre-Early-Access update. They match everything observed since launch, but each line is still pending direct re-verification on 0.8.10.562.

sections.heading: Known limitations
sections.text: Video observations on this page were recorded on build 0.8.10.455, the launch build; the current official version is 0.8.10.562. The 0.8.10.562 hotfix touched animals and vehicles, not farming systems, but we label the observation build explicitly rather than merging the two.

sections.heading: Known limitations
sections.text: The ~3-day dry-out timer and the 7-field watering can / 25-field advanced sprinkler coverage numbers are community-reported; the season-seed list is a single community report.

sections.heading: Known limitations
sections.text: Sprinkler hookup (water/power), the tilling tool flow, and greenhouse unlock rules are open questions — see the hold section .

sections.heading: Farming FAQ
sections.text: Do I have to water crops every day?

sections.heading: Farming FAQ
sections.text: Not verified yet for planted crops. Corroborated player reports only establish that an empty, unseeded tilled plot can revert after roughly three dry days and that rain counts. Do not use that timer as a crop-watering schedule until a current-build test records plant condition over several days.

sections.heading: Farming FAQ
sections.text: What happens if I forget to harvest?

sections.heading: Farming FAQ
sections.text: Per the official pre-Early-Access mechanics update (Dec 2, 2025), fruit and vegetables are no longer destroyed merely because you forgot to harvest, and seeds only disappear when the plant itself dies. Current-build players also report crop loss around season changes; one reply gives day 30 → day 1 as the cutoff, but that exact timing still needs reproduction. The cautious move is to finish seasonal harvests before rollover.

sections.heading: Farming FAQ
sections.text: Is fertilizer worth buying?

sections.heading: Farming FAQ
sections.text: The Aug 4 support warning said fertilizer was calculating incorrectly and advised players to avoid investing until it was adjusted. The 0.8.10.562 notes did not announce a fix, but we have not re-tested the item on that build. Avoid a large purchase until current evidence confirms its return.

sections.heading: Farming FAQ
sections.text: How do I make a new field, and how do I get a greenhouse?

sections.heading: Farming FAQ
sections.text: Both are on hold. The only tilling walkthroughs are from the 2022 Alpha, and the only greenhouse unlock reference (blueprint from Lina) is from November 2022 — neither is verified for the current build. We have published the exact verification steps in the hold section instead of guessing.

(Dec 2, 2025), states the new plantation rules directly: Seeds only disappear when the plant dies. A planted seed is not consumed by harvesting or by time alone. Fruits and vegetables no longer get destroyed if you forget to harvest them. Ripe produce waits on the plant instead of rotting away. A simpler, more intuitive re-grow flow for recurring crops. Because this wording comes from an official update and no later patch note (through 0.8.10.562) contradicts it, we treat these as the working rules — with the explicit caveat that they were announced before Early Access launch and we have not yet re-verified each line in-game on the current build.

title: Season-change crop loss: current reports, exact cutoff unverified
parentTitle: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: Current-build reports Two current-build threads report crops disappearing around a season boundary, but they do not independently establish every calendar detail. In "WTF ?? A whole field of eggplants gone after sleeping ???" (Aug 3, 2026), the poster lost an entire eggplant field overnight; player Mancer explained that day 30 is the last harvest day, day 1 begins the new season, and seasonal crops are removed during the rollover. FIDELIS reported disappearing eggplants in "Things disappear" (Aug 6), but that report alone does not verif Mancer's season-seed list from the same thread is a single community report, so treat it as a working reference, not gospel: summer — green lettuce, eggplant, corn; spring — strawberries, garlic, green salad; autumn — onions, carrots, pumpkins. Our own video-observed data confirms strawberry as a spring seed and red lettuce with a spring tag on build 0.8.10.455 (see the crop database ). Practical takeaway: check the calendar before a big planting run late in a season — seeds planted on day 28 of a season may never reach their first harvest.

title: Regrow vs one-time crops
parentTitle: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: Video-observed recorded on build 0.8.10.455 Retained gameplay footage of the launch build shows the two crop archetypes side by side: Strawberry Seeds (144C): spring seed, first harvest 7 days after planting, then re-harvests every 3 days — a recurring crop. Red Lettuce Seeds (48C): spring seed, matures in 3 days with no regrow line on the seed description — a one-time crop you replant. The official pre-EA update's "simpler re-grow flow for recurring crops" Official matches this split: recurring crops keep their plant and cycle again, one-time crops are replanted from new seeds. Exact regrow intervals for other crops are still being collected — the crop database tracks each one with its own evidence label.

title: Watering: what is known and what is not
parentTitle: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: Empty plots corroborated Tools official pre-EA update Two independent discussion threads answer why empty tilled plots disappear. In "Agricultural fields?!" (Jul 31, 2026), players say unwatered, unseeded plots vanish after a few days; in "Removing Farming Patches?" (Jul 31), another player estimates about 3 days without rain, watering or crops/weeds and says rain counts. These reports do not establish how often a planted crop must be watered, so this page no longer turns the empty-plot timer into crop-care advice. The same Dec 2, 2025 official update also confirms the watering toolset exists and was tuned: sprinkler timings adjusted to water plantations more quickly , and a larger area of effect for the watering can Official pre-EA . Launch-build footage shows three sprinkler tiers and a water well in the crafting menu's farming tab Video-observed build 0.8.10.455 . One German-language player report mentions a watering can covering about 7 fields and an advanced sprinkler covering 25 — a Single report we have not corroborate What we do not know yet: how a sprinkler connects to water or power (pipe, cable, well radius or none) is not shown in any retained source, so we deliberately do not print hookup instructions. Treat sprinkler placement as finicky too — one player calls placement "still wonky" ( same thread , single report).

title: Selling your harvest
parentTitle: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: Harvests are sold through the CashIn chest : deposit produce during the day and the money lands as the "Farming" line of the end-of-day settlement, which does not break down per crop. The full observed workflow — linking the chest, depositing, and reading the bill — is documented step by step in the money-making guide's CashIn section , so we do not repeat it here. The Dec 2, 2025 update also mentions an economy pass with fruit, vegetable and seed prices adjusted Official pre-EA , which is why we never quote Alpha-era price lists as current values. Per-crop sell prices remain unknown while the settlement screen stays aggregated — see the crop database for what is measured versus pending.

title: Fertilizer: official warning, current behavior pending
parentTitle: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: Official warning issued Aug 4, 2026; 0.8.10.562 behavior not re-tested In "Furtilizer not worth it" (Aug 3, 2026), a player documented spending 8,000C on legendary fertilizer that covered 8 of 24 plots and netted only 79C of extra profit. Support moderator Jennoula replied on Aug 4, 2026: "we are aware that the fertilizer is not currently calculating correctly and it is being looked into, so for now just avoid investing in fertilizer until we get it adjusted again." The 0.8.10.562 hotfix notes (Aug 10, 2026) do not announce a fertilizer fix , but omission from patch notes is not proof that behavior stayed unchanged. We have not re-tested fertilizer on 0.8.10.562. Until a current-build test or official reply confirms the calculation was adjusted, the cautious recommendation is to avoid a large fertilizer investment . Fertilizer is still visible in the shop (Leafy Market's Seed & Fertilizer tab, video-observed on 0.8.10.455) — availability does not verify its return.

title: How do you open a new field? (Hold)
parentTitle: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: Historical Unverified lead The only hoe-based tilling account on record is from the 2022 Alpha (a player buying seeds and a hoe, planting and watering daily) — useful as a hint that a hoe tool is involved, but two major versions out of date. Current-build evidence only proves the mechanic is called "tilling" and that tilled plots revert to normal ground on their own (a feedback thread asks for a way to undo tilling, Aug 6, 2026; the dry-out threads above). Launch-build footage shows three "foundation"-type items in the crafting menu's farmin Planned verification (not yet done): buy the hoe at the seed shop, use it on open ground, record the exact prompts and whether a plot appears; then place each of the three farming-tab "foundation" items and document what they create. Until that is recorded, any step-by-step "how to till" you read elsewhere — including anything we could write — is unverified.

parentTitle: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: Historical Single report The greenhouse appears in official materials as one of the ways to build out the farm, and one current-build player (Mancer, in the eggplant thread ) reports that greenhouses allow out-of-season planting , saying they tested planting in winter with one — a single self-reported test, not yet corroborated. The only unlock-path evidence on record is from November 2022 : the developers confirmed back then that the greenhouse blueprint was sold by Lina and required both materials and money. Whether that vendor, price an Planned verification (not yet done): check Lina's blueprint list on the current build for a greenhouse entry and its material cost; if built, test an out-of-season seed inside and record the result.

title: Farming FAQ
parentTitle: Farming & Fields in The Ranchers: Watering, Harvest, Regrow and Fertilizer Rules
description: Do I have to water crops every day? Not verified yet for planted crops. Corroborated player reports only establish that an empty, unseeded tilled plot can revert after roughly three dry days and that rain counts. Do not use that timer as a crop-watering schedule until a current-build test records plant condition over several days. What happens if I forget to harvest? Per the official pre-Early-Access mechanics update (Dec 2, 2025), fruit and vegetables are no longer destroyed merely because you forgot to harvest, and seeds only disappear when the plant itself dies. Current-build players also report crop loss around season changes; one reply gives day 30 → day 1 as the cutoff, but that exact timing still needs reproduction. The cautious move is to finish seasonal harvests before rollover. Is fertilizer worth buying? The Aug 4 support warning said fertilizer was calculating incorrectly and advised players to avoid investing until it was adjusted. The 0.8.10.562 notes did not announce a fix, but we have not re-tested the item on that build. Avoid a large purchase until current evidence confirms its return. How do I make a new field, and how do I get a greenhouse? Both are on hold. The only tilling walkthroughs are from the 2022 Alpha, and the only greenhouse unlock reference (blueprint from Lina) is from November 2022 — neither is verified for the current build. We have published the exact verification steps in the hold section instead of guessing.

sections.text: Updated for Early Access 0.8.10.x (August 2026) · August 7, 2026 · Reading time: ~6 min

sections.heading: Answer first
sections.text: The Ranchers controls were simplified in an official update: Right Mouse Button rotates the camera, Left Mouse Button performs all primary tool actions, and building placement with the Hammer now needs only one button . Open the menu with ESC — Game Settings, including the full Camera Settings section, are accessible directly from it. Every default value and its source update is listed below.

sections.heading: Controls quick reference
sections.text: Official Day rollover is manual. Per the pre-EA Ranching v2 update notes, a new day starts only when you press the "Start new day" button in the end-of-the-day summary — the notes explicitly call this the way to pause the game, and say it works in multiplayer too. Caveat: this is pre-EA official documentation , not yet independently rechecked in the current EA build. If you need a break mid-day, use sleep to reach the summary screen and simply do not press the button until you are ready.

sections.heading: Building controls
sections.text: The same update added clearer error messages when placing blueprints — for unpurchased farm parcels, unauthorized zones or interiors, collisions or failed placement requirements, and exceeding City Hall building height limits. If placement fails, read the message before assuming a bug; see the Building & Placement Guide and the roof quest troubleshooting page for the most common blockers.

sections.heading: Motion sickness: settings that help
sections.text: Editorial The suggestions in this section are our editorial recommendations, built on the official settings above — they are not official prescriptions.

sections.heading: Motion sickness: settings that help
sections.text: Adjust Automatic Camera Recentering Latency first. The official notes explicitly say this setting (default 0.5 s) helps with motion sickness — a lower value recenters the camera faster.

sections.heading: Motion sickness: settings that help
sections.text: Keep Auto Reset Camera Zoom disabled (the default) so the frame stays stable while driving instead of zooming on context changes.

sections.heading: Motion sickness: settings that help
sections.text: Decide on recentering deliberately. If automatic camera movement bothers you, disable Automatic Camera Recenter – In Vehicle; if fighting the camera manually is what tires you, enable the on-foot recenter instead.

sections.heading: Motion sickness: settings that help
sections.text: Lower Camera Movement Speed if fast panning is what triggers discomfort — the post-update camera already has reduced acceleration and deceleration, so small slider changes go a long way.

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: How do I rotate the camera in The Ranchers?

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: Hold the Right Mouse Button, per the official control simplification update (Feb 2026, demo-era — recheck against the current EA build). All primary tool actions moved to the Left Mouse Button at the same time.

sections.heading: Controls FAQ

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: Open the menu with ESC — Game Settings are accessible directly from the ESC menu — and look for the dedicated Camera Settings section added in the Feb 2026 update (demo-era; recheck against the current EA build).

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: Does the game pause when I open Settings?

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: In solo mode, yes — the official notes say the game pauses while you use the Feedback App or Settings App (Feb 2026 update, demo-era; recheck against the current EA build). Do not rely on pausing in a co-op session.

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: Is there QWERTZ keyboard support?

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: Yes — QWERTZ layout support (Germany, Austria, etc.) was added in the official Feb 2026 update (demo-era; recheck against the current EA build).

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: The camera keeps swinging back while I drive. Can I stop it?

sections.heading: Controls FAQ
sections.text: That is Automatic Camera Recenter – In Vehicle, which is enabled by default. Disable it in Camera Settings, or raise the recentering latency (default 0.5 s) so it kicks in more slowly.

title: Camera settings, one by one
parentTitle: The Ranchers Controls & Camera Settings Guide
description: Official A dedicated Camera Settings section was added in the Feb 2026 update (demo-era); recheck against the current EA build. The same update also reduced camera acceleration and deceleration to remove the "snapping" effect, making movement smoother and more predictable. The settings and their official defaults: Our suggestion Editorial Camera Movement Speed How fast the camera turns with your input Start at default; raise it only if the camera feels like it lags behind your mouse How fast zoom responds Leave at default unless zooming feels jumpy while driving Automatic Camera Recenter – On Foot When enabled, the camera automatically rotates to align with the player's direction, without manual input Keep it off if you like full manual control; try enabling it if you find yourself constantly dragging the camera while walking Automatic Camera Recenter – In Vehicle Same auto-alignment while driving The default-on behavior suits most driving; disable it only if you prefer to watch the ranch while cruising Automatic Camera Recentering Latency Controls how quickly the camera realigns — lower value = faster recentering. The official notes say this setting helps with motion sickness If the game makes you queasy, this is the first slider to experiment with — see motion sickness below Auto Reset Camera Zoom When enabled, zoom adjusts automatically depending on context; when disabled, zoom remains stable while driving Keep it off (the default) for a stable frame while driving; enable it only if you want automatic zoom changes between contexts

description: Official (Feb 2026 update, demo-era); recheck against the current EA build. Two options were added for builders: Auto Equip Hammer after placement — default ON. The Hammer stays in your hands after placing a blueprint, so chaining multiple placements does not require re-equipping. Auto Re-Equip Same Blueprint after placement — default OFF. title: Motion sickness: settings that help
parentTitle: The Ranchers Controls & Camera Settings Guide
description: Editorial The suggestions in this section are our editorial recommendations, built on the official settings above — they are not official prescriptions. Adjust Automatic Camera Recentering Latency first. The official notes explicitly say this setting (default 0.5 s) helps with motion sickness — a lower value recenters the camera faster. Keep Auto Reset Camera Zoom disabled (the default) so the frame stays stable while driving instead of zooming on context changes. Decide on recentering deliberately. If automatic camera movement bothers you, disable Automatic Camera Recenter – In Vehicle; if fighting the camera manually is what tires you, enable the on-foot recenter instead. Lower Camera Movement Speed if fast panning is what triggers discomfort — the post-update camera already has reduced acceleration and deceleration, so small slider changes go a long way.

title: Controls FAQ
parentTitle: The Ranchers Controls & Camera Settings Guide
description: How do I rotate the camera in The Ranchers? Hold the Right Mouse Button, per the official control simplification update (Feb 2026, demo-era — recheck against the current EA build). All primary tool actions moved to the Left Mouse Button at the same time. Where are the camera settings? Open the menu with ESC — Game Settings are accessible directly from the ESC menu — and look for the dedicated Camera Settings section added in the Feb 2026 update (demo-era; recheck against the current EA build). Does the game pause when I open Settings? In solo mode, yes — the official notes say the game pauses while you use the Feedback App or Settings App (Feb 2026 update, demo-era; recheck against the current EA build). Do not rely on pausing in a co-op session. Is there QWERTZ keyboard support? Yes — QWERTZ layout support (Germany, Austria, etc.) was added in the official Feb 2026 update (demo-era; recheck against the current EA build). The camera keeps swinging back while I drive. Can I stop it? That is Automatic Camera Recenter – In Vehicle, which is enabled by default. Disable it in Camera Settings, or raise the recentering latency (default 0.5 s) so it kicks in more slowly.

title: Strawberry
description: Database record: fruit Strawberry Updated 2026-08-08 The first video-confirmed regrow crop: 144C seed, Spring, 7 days to first harvest, then fruit every 3 days. Berry sell price is unobserved — the 18C-per-harvest figure is a cost-allocation model, not revenue. Seed source & price Strawberry Seed is sold in the Leafy Market "Seed & Fertilizer" tab at 144C (Basic quality); the purchase dialog separately confirmed 10 seeds = 1,440C. Video-observed Games Station gameplay footage V0.8.10.455 (local archive: games-station.mp4, seed tab 03:15–03:50, CashIn 59:41–59:57) The historical Alpha record listed Strawberry Seeds at 38C — superseded by the current-build 144C observation; kept as a lead only. Historical Farmer's Land — community-maintained player wiki page (Alpha build) Growth & regrow Season: Spring · Growth time: 7 days · Multi-harvest: every 3 days (regrows after the first harvest). Video-observed Games Station gameplay footage V0.8.10.455 (local archive: games-station.mp4, seed tab 03:15–03:50, CashIn 59:41–59:57) The historical Alpha record claimed daily fruiting after maturity with 10-20 berries per plot and a 20C sale value — Alpha data, not confirmed in the current build. Historical Farmer's Land — community-maintained player wiki page (Alpha build) Sell price (player) vs retail Theoretical model (our derivation, not an observed outcome): seed-cost allocation ≈ 18C per harvest, assuming eight harvests in a full 30-day Spring (day 7, then days 10, 13, 16, 19, 22, 25, 28) with no missed regrowth, no season-boundary loss and no plant death. Profit/day = (sell price × yield − allocated seed cost) ÷ 3 — open until a sell price is captured. title: Fertilizer
description: Database record: farm input Fertilizer Updated 2026-08-08 Officially flagged as miscalculating in the current build — the official advice is to avoid investing until it is fixed.
